Nothing warns before the listener closes. close_after x interval (5 s at the defaults) is shorter than any scrape interval, so no alert can fire between the first failed health check and the close. port49_store_health_failures_close pages once the listeners are closed: the gauge is held by the process, not the run, so the page stays raised through the whole outage and resolves when the listeners reopen.

Series that exist only where the thing does. port49_store_directory_reachable, port49_store_directory_confirmed_timestamp_seconds, port49_store_keyspace_held and port49_directory_refresh_last_complete_timestamp_seconds are created by the code that starts what they watch (the etcd store, the keyspace runner, the scheduled refresh), at 0. On the memory backend, the default, they do not exist, so no alert on == 0 or on age has a series to fire on. Where a gauge cannot work that way, a *_configured gauge says whether to expect it: port49_issuing_ca_configured, port49_directory_password_configured.

Where the rules differ from the statement they answer. - port49_oidc_keys_stale drops the statement's or absent(): every configured issuer's series is created at 0, so an issuer that never fetched already shows time() - 0, and the series is absent only where OIDC is not configured, where absent() would fire forever. - port49_directory_enrollment_store_lost keeps it, as port49_directory_password_configured == 1 unless on(instance) port49_directory_enrollment_store_ok: the gauge is absent until the store first answers, and a broker that never reached it is the case to catch. - port49_issuing_ca_expiring also requires the CA gauge above 0, so the page for a missing CA is not doubled by a ticket for a CA "expiring" in 1970. - port49_store_directory_stale requires its timestamp above 0 (a process that has not yet confirmed is port49_store_directory_unreachable and port49_store_feed_down). - port49_directory_refresh_stale and port49_directory_refresh_half_ceiling take the freshest refresh across all runner-capable replicas, so a replica that lost the hold, whose gauge stops moving, does not alarm; and they require the newest such process to have been up as long as the threshold, so a restart is quiet but a restart in the middle of a directory outage (the gauge reads 0 until a pass completes) still fires. Both wait 15 minutes (for:), which covers a runner failover: the new runner's series sits at 0 until its first pass completes. They read last_over_time(...[1d]), so they keep firing for a day after every broker is gone, when no series is left to read. - port49_inventory_snapshot_stale is the spec's expression with its NaN arm and no gate: a process that never watches the inventory reads 0, and one waiting for its first snapshot reads NaN before its listener opens, which is the case the NaN arm exists for. - port49_store_keyspace_unheld sums over the processes that run a keyspace runner, and fires for a day after the last one disappears (a crashed fleet exports no 0): count(last_over_time(...[1d])) unless count(...). A memory-backend install never had the series, so it never fires. - The key-retirement rules leave out the spec's uptime gate (spec, key rotation: line 5578). That only makes them fire more. A restart blanks port49_key_version_devices (it counts devices whose latest validated connection since start used the version), so a rule that resolves after a restart is not evidence the devices have moved: read the decision log. - enrolled sign-ins outside a rollout are not alerted: "outside a rollout" is yours to define.

docs.title: port49_target_down
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: 2m.

A port49d or broker target is not answering its scrape: up is 0 for it.

up{job=~"port49d|port49-broker"} == 0

Source: A port49d or broker that is down raises no alarm of its own, because every other rule reads series it no longer exports

Why this threshold: up == 0 for a scrape target of either job; two minutes outlasts a restart's missed scrapes.

docs.title: port49_target_absent
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: 5m.

Prometheus has no up series for port49d: no port49d target exists at all, so every device has lost port49 and falls to local authentication, and no other port49d rule can fire.

absent(up{job="port49d"})

Source: A port49d target Prometheus is not scraping at all has no up series, so == 0 never matches

Why this threshold: absent() of port49d's up. Prometheus's pod discovery keeps a target only while its pod exists, so a StatefulSet with every pod Pending or deleted leaves no series for == 0 to match, and every device has lost port49: a page. Five minutes outlasts a rollout. A mislabelled scrape config shows here too.

docs.title: port49_broker_target_absent
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

Prometheus has no up series for the broker: no broker target exists at all, so no token can be minted and no other broker rule can fire.

absent(up{job="port49-broker"})

Source: The same for the broker: no up series for port49-broker at all

Why this threshold: absent() of the broker's up: no token can be minted, but held tokens still log in. On the memory-store trial, which runs no separate broker, the broker rule fires; drop it there or silence it.

docs.title: port49_global_cap_shedding
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

port49d reset TACACS+ connections at accept because the global connection cap was full; devices fall to local authentication.

increase(port49_connections_shed_total{reason="global_cap"}[5m]) > 0

Source: Connections reset at accept because the global connection cap is full: port49_connections_shed_total{reason="global_cap"} increasing

Why this threshold: Any shed connection is a device refused, so any increase pages; five minutes smooths one scrape.

docs.title: port49_connections_near_cap
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

A port49d is holding more than 80% of limits.max_connections open; raise the cap or add replicas before it sheds.

sum by (instance) (port49_connections{state="open"}) / on(instance) port49_connections_max > 0.8

Source: A warning before shedding starts: port49_connections near the cap

Why this threshold: Ten minutes at 80% is a trend, not a burst; the page above covers the cap itself.

docs.title: port49_token_clock_skew
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A port49d read a token minted more than a second ahead of its own clock: a broker's clock runs ahead of this host's. Put every broker and port49d host on NTP; a broker clock behind by a token_ttl mints tokens that are dead on arrival.

increase(port49_token_minted_ahead_total[15m]) > 0

Source: A broker's clock runs ahead of a port49d's: port49_token_minted_ahead_total increasing

Why this threshold: Expiry on etcd is the record's, read against port49d's clock, so a skewed pair shifts every token's life by the skew. A token minted more than a second in port49d's future is read directly from the record. A broker behind by a token_ttl cannot be seen this way (its tokens are dead on arrival); the fix is the same, NTP on every broker and port49d host.

docs.title: port49_key_secret_files_changed
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

A key version's secret file changed or cannot be read; the held secret stays in force until the next start.

port49_key_secret_files_changed > 0

Source: A key version's secret file that changed or cannot be read: port49_key_secret_files_changed > 0 for 10m

Why this threshold: A rotated file is expected for minutes while the rollout restarts; ten minutes is a forgotten restart.

docs.title: port49_issuing_ca_missing
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: 5m.

A broker is configured to issue certificates and has no usable issuing CA, so every OIDC sign-in is refused issuance_unavailable; run port49d init-issuer or restore the CA.

port49_issuing_ca_not_after_timestamp_seconds == 0 and on(instance) port49_issuing_ca_configured == 1

Source: A broker set to issue certificates that has no usable issuing CA: port49_issuing_ca_not_after_timestamp_seconds == 0 while broker.identity.issuance is configured

Why this threshold: A broker started without its CA says so and keeps serving; five minutes outlasts a rollout and nothing else clears it.

docs.title: port49_issuing_ca_expiring
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

The issuing CA expires within 90 days; make its successor and distribute the new bundle before sign-ins stop.

(port49_issuing_ca_not_after_timestamp_seconds - time() < 90 * 86400) and on(instance) (port49_issuing_ca_not_after_timestamp_seconds > 0) and on(instance) port49_issuing_ca_configured == 1

Source: The issuing CA expires within 90 days

Why this threshold: Ninety days is a CA rollover's lead time; a CA already at 0 is the page above, not this ticket.

docs.title: port49_key_retirement_within_7d
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A key version with devices still on it passes its retire_after within 7 days; move the devices (the decision log names them) before it does.

(port49_key_version_devices > 0) and on(key_ref, version) (port49_key_retirement_seconds < 7 * 86400)

Source: A key version that devices still present nears its retire_after: the first step of an alarm whose severity rises as the date approaches

Why this threshold: A week is a change window; the series carry no device identity, the log names the devices.

docs.title: port49_key_retirement_within_1d
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

A key version with devices still on it passes its retire_after within a day, or already has; those devices fail authentication once it does.

(port49_key_version_devices > 0) and on(key_ref, version) (port49_key_retirement_seconds < 86400)

Source: The same key version within a day of its retire_after, or past it: the alarm's last step

Why this threshold: A day is the last working shift; a version past retire_after with devices on it is refusing them now.

docs.title: port49_admin_touch_refused
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

An admin call was refused its hardware-key touch proof: a stolen token or a broken key.

increase(port49_admin_touch_total{outcome="refused"}[10m]) > 0

Source: An admin call refused its hardware-key touch proof: port49_admin_touch_total{outcome="refused"}

Why this threshold: Someone holds an admin credential without the touch; no benign cause repeats.

docs.title: port49_policy_fail_closed_compositions
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

The policy in force has compositions answered fail-closed: those users are denied all but the allows; port49 policy test names them.

port49_policy_fail_closed_compositions > 0

Source: A policy in force that answers some compositions fail-closed: port49_policy_fail_closed_compositions > 0

Why this threshold: A standing condition of the policy, not an incident; a ticket the author sees.

docs.title: port49_policy_file_refused
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

The policy file on disk was refused or will not settle; an older policy is serving.

port49_policy_file_refused == 1

Source: A policy file on disk that is refused or will not settle: port49_policy_file_refused == 1

Why this threshold: An edit in progress is refused for seconds; five minutes is a file that stayed wrong.

docs.title: port49_policy_refresh_pending
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 2m.

A policy change has not yet reached every live login context.

port49_policy_refresh_pending == 1

Source: A policy swap or grant expiry that has not yet reached every live login context: 1 from the change until its settle pass

Why this threshold: A pass takes seconds; two minutes is a stuck settle pass.

docs.title: port49_policy_bundle_mismatch
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

A broker or port49d serves a policy bundle other than the runner's; its tokens or admissions carry another policy until it reloads.

port49_policy_bundle_matches_runner == 0

Source: A broker serving a policy bundle other than the runner's: port49_policy_bundle_matches_runner 0 for longer than twice broker.policy_watch_interval

Why this threshold: Five minutes outlasts twice the watch interval and the settle delay at their defaults; raise it if the intervals are raised.

docs.title: port49_broker_mint_gate_closed
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 1m.

A broker mints nothing: its mint gate has been closed for over a minute; the store does not answer, or no runner judges its bundle.

port49_broker_mint_gate_closed == 1

Source: A broker that mints nothing: port49_broker_mint_gate_closed at 1 for a minute

Why this threshold: The gate is closed from a start until a takeover is seen, so a minute is where a restart ends and a fault begins; a ticket, since other replicas keep minting.

docs.title: port49_devices_generic_platform
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

Admitted devices are served by the generic adapter: their platform has no adapter, and their commands are judged without its knowledge.

port49_devices_generic_platform > 0

Source: Admitted devices served by the generic adapter: port49_devices_generic_platform, naming no device

Why this threshold: A standing condition of the inventory, not an incident; the start line names the platforms and counts.

docs.title: port49_context_refreshes_failed
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A policy refresh could not carry a login context onto the policy in force: a context revoked for a compile fault, or one that would not open.

increase(port49_context_refreshes_total{outcome="failed"}[10m]) > 0

Source: A login context a policy refresh could not carry onto the policy in force: counted failed in port49_context_refreshes_total

Why this threshold: Each failure is one context left on an older policy or revoked.

docs.title: port49_per_login_mfa_refused
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

A run of per-login MFA proofs did not verify: someone is trying another token or another person's sign-in.

increase(port49_per_login_mfa_total{outcome="refused"}[10m]) > 2

Source: A run of per-login MFA proofs that did not verify: per_login_mfa_refused, alerted on its own, because a run of them is someone trying another token or another person's sign-in

Why this threshold: More than two in ten minutes is a run; a mistyped touch is one.

docs.title: port49_store_directory_unreachable
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: 1m.

This process cannot read the directory store: revocations and password sign-ins from other regions do not arrive.

port49_store_directory_reachable == 0

Source: A process that cannot read the directory store: port49_store_directory_reachable == 0 for 1m

Why this threshold: A cut region keeps logging devices in on stale marks, so one minute is a real partition.

docs.title: port49_store_directory_stale
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 1m.

This process last confirmed its copy of the directory store over a minute ago, whatever the reason; its revocation marks may be stale.

(time() - port49_store_directory_confirmed_timestamp_seconds > 60) and on(instance) port49_store_directory_confirmed_timestamp_seconds > 0

Source: A process whose copy of the directory store is unconfirmed for over a minute: time() - port49_store_directory_confirmed_timestamp_seconds > 60

Why this threshold: The series exists only under etcd, at 0 until the first confirmation, so a 0 is skipped here: port49_store_directory_unreachable and port49_store_feed_down cover a process that never confirmed.

docs.title: port49_store_logouts_pending
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

Back-channel logouts were accepted while the directory store did not answer and have not reached it.

port49_store_logouts_pending > 0

Source: Back-channel logouts accepted but not yet in the directory store: port49_store_logouts_pending > 0 for 5m

Why this threshold: A cut region holds logouts the others have not seen; five minutes is longer than a blip.

docs.title: port49_store_marks_feed_down
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: 1m.

The marks feed is down: revocation marks written elsewhere do not reach this process.

port49_store_feed_up{feed="marks"} == 0

Source: The marks feed down, so revocation marks written elsewhere do not arrive: port49_store_feed_up{feed="marks"} == 0

Why this threshold: Revocation rides this feed; a minute is four times the 15s hold_ttl default and the longest hold_ttl allows (10s to 1m), so at any setting the feed has been down for a full hold.

docs.title: port49_store_feed_down
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 1m.

A store feed other than marks is down (contexts, or a split broker's pins or logouts): this process misses other replicas' writes, and its directory copy is not confirmed.

port49_store_feed_up{feed!="marks"} == 0

Source: A store feed other than marks down: port49_store_feed_up{feed} 0 for longer than hold_ttl

Why this threshold: A minute is four times the 15s hold_ttl default and the longest hold_ttl allows (10s to 1m). Every feed but marks, which pages, so a feed added later is covered.

docs.title: port49_store_feed_legs_colocated
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

Both legs of the {{ $labels.feed }} feed's watch are on one etcd member: port49 reaches only one etcd member for this feed, so check the other members; that member going dark stalls the feed.

port49_store_feed_legs_colocated == 1

Source: Both legs of a feed's watch on one etcd member: port49_store_feed_legs_colocated at 1 for 10m

Why this threshold: Both legs of a feed's watch on one member is no redundancy against that member going dark; the move apart is tried from 2 s doubling to 30 s, so ten minutes is a cluster where no other member is reachable for this feed. A client with one etcd endpoint never moves a leg and holds the gauge at 0 (colocation is not a fault there); port49d logs once at start that the feeds share one member.

docs.title: port49_store_circuit_open
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 1m.

A store pool's circuit is open: its calls fail at once until a probe succeeds.

port49_store_circuit_open == 1

Source: A store pool's circuit open, so its calls fail at once

Why this threshold: The rule fires for every {component, pool} series, and what an open circuit costs depends on which. On port49d (component="daemon"), a token or context pool open for hold_ttl (the 15s hold_ttl default) closes the listeners, so a minute is four times that and this ticket follows the close; it does not warn before it. A bulk pool never closes them: logins and commands are unaffected and the scans (the refresh, a revocation by principal, a start's purge) fail until a probe succeeds. On port49-broker (component="broker") no circuit closes anything, because its guards never stop; mints, refreshes and revocations through the open pool fail. The component broker_enrollments refuses password sign-in and second-factor enrollment through its open pool, and closes nothing.

docs.title: port49_contexts_reindexed
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

Live login contexts were found missing from the index: an index record was deleted in the store.

increase(port49_contexts_reindexed_total[10m]) > 0

Source: Live login contexts found missing from the index: any increase of port49_contexts_reindexed_total

Why this threshold: No benign path deletes an index record.

docs.title: port49_contexts_reindex_failures
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A login context could not be re-indexed or judged; one sealed under a key port49d does not hold is denied, never revoked (check PORT49_ENC_V1).

increase(port49_contexts_reindex_failures_total[10m]) > 0

Source: A login context that could not be re-indexed or judged: any increase of port49_contexts_reindex_failures_total

Why this threshold: Each failure leaves a context for the next pass; a mis-set key repeats it.

docs.title: port49_store_calls_refused
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

etcd's roles are refusing port49's store calls; port49d answers store_unavailable.

increase(port49_store_calls_total{outcome="refused"}[10m]) > 0

Source: etcd's roles refusing port49's store calls: any increase of port49_store_calls_total{outcome="refused"}

Why this threshold: A refused call is a role or credential fault that retries cannot fix.

docs.title: port49_store_keyspace_unheld
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 2m.

No port49-broker replica holds the store keyspace: no runner is judging bundles, purging or refreshing contexts.

(sum(port49_store_keyspace_held) == 0) or (count(last_over_time(port49_store_keyspace_held[1d])) unless count(port49_store_keyspace_held))

Source: No broker replica holding the store keyspace: the sum of port49_store_keyspace_held over port49-broker's replicas 0 for twice hold_ttl

Why this threshold: Two minutes is eight times the 15s hold_ttl default, and exactly twice the longest hold_ttl allows (1m), so it holds at any setting. The series exists only on a process that runs a keyspace runner, so the memory backend, with none, raises nothing. The second arm covers every broker gone (a crashed fleet exports no 0): series seen in the last day and none now, so it fires for a day after the brokers vanish, then stops.

docs.title: port49_store_client_cert_expiring
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A component's etcd client certificate expires within 30 days.

port49_store_client_cert_expiry_timestamp_seconds - time() < 30 * 86400

Source: A store client certificate within 30 days of expiry

Why this threshold: Thirty days is the stated lead time.

docs.title: port49_crypt_store_key_unknown
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

port49d started on a store last written under a current key its encryption window does not hold (a mis-set PORT49_ENC_V1).

port49_crypt_store_key_unknown == 1

Source: port49d started on a store written under a key its encryption window does not hold: port49_crypt_store_key_unknown at 1

Why this threshold: Records written under the missing key cannot open; fix the key and start again.

docs.title: port49_crypt_token_open_failures
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A stored token would not decrypt: a rotation may have retired a key while tokens it sealed were live.

increase(port49_crypt_open_failures_total{record="token"}[10m]) > 0

Source: A stored token that would not decrypt: any increase of port49_crypt_open_failures_total{record="token"}

Why this threshold: The counter is the only witness; the token is dropped from its candidates with no error.

docs.title: port49_directory_pins_unopenable
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A directory pin opens under neither encryption key: its principal cannot bind, mint or refresh.

port49_directory_pins_unopenable > 0 and on(instance) port49_store_keyspace_held == 1

Source: A directory pin that opens under neither encryption key: port49_directory_pins_unopenable above 0 on the replica holding the keyspace

Why this threshold: One principal is locked out until the key that sealed the pin is back as encryption.previous or the pin is forgotten; the pass never deletes it. Gated on port49_store_keyspace_held == 1, since a replica that handed over keeps its last value.

docs.title: port49_store_feed_rescans
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A feed's watch was compacted and rescanned the store; the feed lagged.

increase(port49_store_feed_rescans_total[10m]) > 0

Source: A feed whose watch was compacted and rescanned the store: any increase of port49_store_feed_rescans_total

Why this threshold: A rescan means a watch fell behind compaction; repeated, the feed is too slow.

docs.title: port49_ledger_pending
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 1m.

The runner's ledger record is behind: a context put back at one would be taken after a restart.

port49_ledger_pending > 0

Source: The runner's ledger record behind: port49_ledger_pending above 0 for a minute

Why this threshold: A write takes a round trip; a minute is a record that cannot be written.

docs.title: port49_ledger_behind
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 1m.

The runner's ledger keeper runs with its context feed down; the record does not follow other processes' logins.

port49_ledger_behind == 1

Source: The runner's ledger keeper running with its context feed down: port49_ledger_behind at 1

Why this threshold: One minute rides out a feed reconnect.

docs.title: port49_store_health_failures_close
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

port49d closed its TACACS+ listeners: its store health checks failed close_after times in a row. Break-glass logins use local passwords until it reopens.

port49_store_health_failures >= 5

Source: port49d closing its TACACS+ listeners after its store health checks fail: port49_store_health_failures >= <close_after>

Why this threshold: 5 is close_after at its default; set it to yours. The gauge is held through the outage, so the page stays up and resolves when the listeners reopen. Not above 0: a defragmenting member fails an occasional check. close_after x interval is shorter than any scrape, so nothing warns first.

docs.title: port49_store_health_check_failing
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

port49d's store health checks are failing often, short of closing the listeners.

increase(port49_store_health_checks_total{outcome="fail"}[10m]) > 60

Source: Store health checks failing often, short of closing the listeners: increase(port49_store_health_checks_total{outcome="fail"}[10m]) above a threshold the operator picks

Why this threshold: At the default 1s interval 60 is a tenth of the checks in ten minutes; a defragmenting member measured 4 to 7 of 18. Set your own.

docs.title: port49_context_cache_stale
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A replica is answering commands from login contexts the store did not confirm; revocation does not reach them until the store answers or the listeners close.

increase(port49_context_cache_lookups_total{outcome="stale"}[5m]) > 0

Source: Commands answered from login contexts the store did not confirm: any increase of port49_context_cache_lookups_total{outcome="stale"}

Why this threshold: Every stale read is a command authorized on unconfirmed state.

docs.title: port49_tls_handshake_failures
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

RFC 9887 listener handshakes are failing; the outcome label says why.

sum by (outcome) (rate(port49_tls_handshakes_total{outcome!~"ok|resumed"}[5m])) > 0

Source: TLS listener handshakes failing, by outcome: rate(port49_tls_handshakes_total{outcome!~"ok\|resumed"}[5m])

Why this threshold: Scanners cause the odd failure; five minutes of them is a device or a certificate.

docs.title: port49_tls_device_certificate_renewal_late
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A device certificate is past two thirds of its own lifetime: its renewal is late. The ratio is the least over certificates verified in the last 24h, so it clears up to a day after the device renews.

port49_tls_device_certificate_lifetime_left_ratio < 0.33

Source: A device certificate whose renewal is late: port49_tls_device_certificate_lifetime_left_ratio < 0.33

Why this threshold: 0.33 is the default expiry_warning_fraction; a ratio holds for any lifetime, a fixed number of days would fire forever on short-lived certificates.

docs.title: port49_tls_server_certificate_renewal_late
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

The RFC 9887 listener's certificate is past two thirds of its own lifetime: its renewal is late.

port49_tls_server_certificate_lifetime_left_ratio < 0.33

Source: The TLS listener's certificate, its renewal late: port49_tls_server_certificate_lifetime_left_ratio < 0.33

Why this threshold: As for the device certificates.

docs.title: port49_tls_server_certificate_expired
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

The RFC 9887 listener's certificate has expired; TLS devices cannot connect.

port49_tls_server_certificate_lifetime_left_ratio < 0

Source: The TLS listener's certificate expired: port49_tls_server_certificate_lifetime_left_ratio < 0 pages

Why this threshold: Below 0 is expired.

docs.title: port49_tls_cert_status_unavailable
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

The TLS listener could not establish a certificate's revocation status; with on_unavailable: refuse its devices are refused.

increase(port49_cert_status_unavailable_total{component="tls_listener"}[10m]) > 0

Source: The TLS listener unable to establish a certificate's revocation status: increase(port49_cert_status_unavailable_total{component="tls_listener"}[10m]) > 0 while TLS devices are admitted

Why this threshold: The series carries only the component; with no TLS devices admitted it does not move.

docs.title: port49_crl_next_update_passed
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A CRL the TLS listener relies on passes its next update within an hour, or has.

time() - port49_crl_next_update_timestamp_seconds{component="tls_listener"} > -3600

Source: A CRL the TLS listener relies on within an hour of its next update, or past it: time() - port49_crl_next_update_timestamp_seconds{component="tls_listener"} > -3600

Why this threshold: An hour is time to fix a failed fetch before the list stops serving.

docs.title: port49_inventory_transport_changed
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A sync changed a device's transport, which may be a downgrade from tls to tcp; port49 records it and does not block it.

increase(port49_inventory_changes_total{kind="transport_changed"}[1h]) > 0

Source: A sync that changed a device's transport: increase(port49_inventory_changes_total{kind="transport_changed"}[1h]) > 0

Why this threshold: A downgrade is silent otherwise.

docs.title: port49_oidc_keys_stale
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

An OIDC issuer's keys were never fetched since this process started, or last fetched over 12h ago, half of jwks_max_age at its default; tokens are refused once they are 24.

time() - port49_oidc_keys_last_success_timestamp_seconds > 12 * 3600

Source: An OIDC provider outage that keeps its keys from being fetched: time() - port49_oidc_keys_last_success_timestamp_seconds > jwks_max_age / 2 or absent(...), with a for: of a few minutes

Why this threshold: Half of jwks_max_age (24h by default): one more failed cycle and every token for that issuer is refused. Set it to yours. Not or absent(): the series exists only for configured issuers, so on a deployment with no OIDC it would fire forever.

docs.title: port49_oidc_logouts_failing
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

OIDC back-channel logouts were not fully applied (store_error or partial); sessions may outlive their sign-out.

increase(port49_oidc_logouts_total{outcome=~"store_error|partial"}[10m]) > 0

Source: OIDC back-channel logouts not fully applied: logouts store_error\|partial

Why this threshold: Each is a logout the store did not take whole.

docs.title: port49_oidc_tokens_unavailable
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

Bearer tokens are refused because their issuer's keys are unavailable.

increase(port49_oidc_tokens_total{outcome="unavailable"}[10m]) > 0

Source: Bearer tokens refused because their issuer's keys are unavailable: tokens unavailable

Why this threshold: The identity provider is unreachable and the held keys have expired.

docs.title: port49_workload_certificates_renewal_late
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

Workload certificates are being presented with under a quarter of their validity left: their renewal is late.

sum(increase(port49_workload_certificates_renewal_late_total[1h])) > 0

Source: Workload certificates presented with their renewal late: increase(port49_workload_certificates_renewal_late_total[1h]) > 0, summed over replicas

Why this threshold: Each replica counts a certificate once per 24h, so any increase of the sum is a late renewer.

docs.title: port49_redemption_restore_unjudged
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: 2m.

port49d cannot read meta/witness, so it cannot tell whether its store was restored, and refuses every token login (store_unavailable) until it can; check the store and the daemon role's read of meta/witness; stopping port49d lets devices fall to break-glass

port49_redemption_restore_unjudged == 1

Source: A port49d that cannot tell whether its store was restored: port49_redemption_restore_unjudged at 1

Why this threshold: The one refusal state the restore floor keeps: port49d cannot read meta/witness, so it refuses every token login with an ERROR, which IOS XE and Junos under tacplus alone treat as final. A failed read clears in seconds; two minutes is a store or a role that stayed wrong.

docs.title: port49_store_restore_detected
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

port49d found its session store restored from a snapshot: tokens minted before the restore are refused token_spent once (users mint again); revocations and marks made after the snapshot are lost: follow the restore runbook, Restoring etcd from a snapshot

(port49_store_restore_detected_timestamp_seconds > 0) and (time() - port49_store_restore_detected_timestamp_seconds < 86400)

Source: A session store restored from a snapshot: port49_store_restore_detected_timestamp_seconds above 0

Why this threshold: Fires for a day after port49d finds its store restored (the gauge holds the time); the restore runbook on the backup and restore page is the work, and revocations made after the snapshot are lost until it is followed. The 0 of a port49d that never found one is skipped.

docs.title: port49_directory_refresh_stale
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 15m.

No scheduled directory refresh has verified every principal for over three refresh intervals; contexts keep their last verification and will deny context_stale at the ceiling.

(time() - max(last_over_time(port49_directory_refresh_last_complete_timestamp_seconds[1d])) > 3 * 300) and on() (time() - max(last_over_time(process_start_time_seconds[1d]) and on(instance) last_over_time(port49_directory_refresh_last_complete_timestamp_seconds[1d])) > 3 * 300)

Source: No scheduled directory refresh completed for three intervals: time() - port49_directory_refresh_last_complete_timestamp_seconds > 3 × refresh_interval

Why this threshold: 300 is broker.refresh_interval at its default (5m); set 3x yours. The freshest refresh anywhere, so a runner that lost the hold does not alarm on its old value; and only once the newest process with the series is also that old, so a restart does not, but a restart in the middle of an outage does (the gauge reads 0 until a pass completes). 15 minutes covers a failover: the new runner's series sits at 0 until its first pass completes. last_over_time keeps the rule firing for a day after every broker is gone.

docs.title: port49_directory_refresh_half_ceiling
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: 15m.

No directory refresh has verified every principal for half of session.staleness_ceiling (4h at its default); at the ceiling every live session denies context_stale. Escapes: session.staleness_ceiling: 0s with a port49d restart, or stop port49d so break-glass applies.

(time() - max(last_over_time(port49_directory_refresh_last_complete_timestamp_seconds[1d])) > 2 * 3600) and on() (time() - max(last_over_time(process_start_time_seconds[1d]) and on(instance) last_over_time(port49_directory_refresh_last_complete_timestamp_seconds[1d])) > 2 * 3600)

Source: No directory refresh completed for half the staleness ceiling: time() - port49_directory_refresh_last_complete_timestamp_seconds > session.staleness_ceiling / 2

Why this threshold: 7200 is half the default ceiling; set half yours. Same shape and 15m for: as port49_directory_refresh_stale. A page: at the ceiling sessions are denied.

docs.title: port49_directory_lookups_ambiguous
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A directory lookup matched more than one principal and was refused identity_ambiguous.

increase(port49_directory_lookups_total{outcome="ambiguous"}[10m]) > 0

Source: Directory lookups that match more than one principal: port49_directory_lookups_total{outcome="ambiguous"} increasing

Why this threshold: Each is a user refused; the directory holds two entries for one name.

docs.title: port49_directory_server_down
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

A directory server's breaker is open; queries go to another server, or fail if there is none.

port49_directory_server_up == 0

Source: A directory server down: port49_directory_server_up == 0 for a while

Why this threshold: Ten minutes: one server down is a degraded pool, not an outage.

docs.title: port49_directory_group_names_ambiguous
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

Group names match no one because two groups under groups_base_dn share them.

port49_directory_group_names_ambiguous > 0

Source: Group names that two directory groups share: port49_directory_group_names_ambiguous > 0

Why this threshold: A gauge over the last hour; the grants naming those groups are not given.

docs.title: port49_directory_enrollment_store_lost
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: 2m.

The broker's password enrollment store is lost, not initialised, or was never reached; password sign-in is refused.

port49_directory_enrollment_store_ok == 0 or (port49_directory_password_configured == 1 unless on(instance) port49_directory_enrollment_store_ok)

Source: The broker's password enrollment store lost or never reached: port49_directory_enrollment_store_ok == 0 or absent()

Why this threshold: The gauge is absent until the store first answers, and a broker that has never reached it is the case to catch. port49_directory_password_configured is 1 only on a broker with the verifier, so a broker without one never matches the absent arm.

docs.title: port49_sign_ins_throttled
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

Directory-password sign-ins are being throttled: failed attempts passed failures_per_principal or failures_per_source.

increase(port49_sign_ins_total{outcome="throttled"}[10m]) > 0

Source: Password sign-ins being throttled: a rise of throttled

Why this threshold: A throttle needs failures_per_* failed attempts: a guessing run, or one user's stale password on a script.

docs.title: port49_sign_ins_enrollment_store_lost
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

A password sign-in was refused because the enrollment store is lost.

increase(port49_sign_ins_total{outcome="enrollment_store_lost"}[10m]) > 0

Source: Password sign-ins refused because the enrollment store is lost: any enrollment_store_lost

Why this threshold: Any one is an operator or user refused; the gauge alert above covers a store that is lost with no sign-in in flight.

docs.title: port49_accounting_spool_drops
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

The accounting spool discarded records; the stage label says where.

increase(port49_accounting_spool_drops_total[10m]) > 0

Source: An accounting spool dropping records

Why this threshold: Accounting records are an audit trail; no drop is acceptable.

docs.title: port49_accounting_spool_disk_slow
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

port49d's accounting spool disk cannot keep up; every accounting record waits on its fsync, so devices see slow or failed accounting. Move the spool directory to a disk with sustained fsync p99 under 10 ms.

histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(port49_accounting_spool_sync_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 0.010

Source: An accounting spool disk too slow, by port49's own threshold: p99 of port49_accounting_spool_sync_seconds over 10 ms for 10m

Why this threshold: Every accounting ack waits on the spool's fsync; with the session etcd and the spool on a CT1000P3PSSD8 drive, account p99 was 152 ms at 170/s (tests/lab/results/load-beehive.md, cell c, step_1_account_p99_ms); with both in RAM the spool's capacity was 1291/s (tests/lab/results/load-beehive-ram.md, cell c), and on a GCE pd-ssd (operator-declared) 2905/s with account p99 3.67 ms at 170/s (tests/lab/results/load-p49-gce-n2s16.us-central1-a.c.port49.internal.md, cell c).

docs.title: port49_decision_log_write_failures
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

The decision log sink refused writes; decisions are not being recorded.

increase(port49_decision_log_write_failures_total[10m]) > 0

Source: Decision log writes refused: the log must be complete, never sampled

Why this threshold: The log is the audit trail; a refused write counts per attempt.

docs.title: port49_accounting_foreign
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: none.

Accounting records arrived for a session port49 never saw begin: a local fallback or console login on a device, or a device bypassing port49.

increase(port49_accounting_attributions_total{attribution="foreign"}[10m]) > 0

Source: Accounting for sessions port49 never saw begin: the foreign series, not rate-limited, because a burst of foreign is itself the signal

Why this threshold: Any foreign record is the detection the spec names for a local login the policy did not see; it pages.

docs.title: port49_inventory_sync_failing
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

The last inventory sync failed: a source, the policy file or the state directory did not answer.

port49_inventory_sync_failing == 1

Source: An inventory sync that failed: the service retains the previous bundle and alarms

Why this threshold: Syncs repeat; ten minutes is several failed ones.

docs.title: port49_inventory_sync_refused
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

The last inventory sync was refused and an older bundle is published.

port49_inventory_sync_refused == 1

Source: An inventory sync that was refused: the service keeps the last good snapshot and alarms

Why this threshold: A refused sync is a bad source document; five minutes is not a race with its fix.

docs.title: port49_inventory_bundle_refused
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

port49d was given an inventory document it refused; the bundle in force keeps serving.

port49_inventory_bundle_refused == 1

Source: An inventory document port49d refused: the fleet keeps the last good snapshot and alarms

Why this threshold: The old bundle serves, so a ticket; five minutes outlasts a rollout.

docs.title: port49_inventory_mirror_behind
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

The inventory mirror's copy differs from the bundle published.

port49_inventory_mirror_behind == 1

Source: The inventory mirror behind the published bundle

Why this threshold: A write is quick; ten minutes behind is a mirror that fails.

docs.title: port49_inventory_persist_failed
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

The inventory document in force could not be written to inventory.service.state_dir; a restart would start without it.

port49_inventory_persist_failed == 1

Source: The inventory document in force not written to the state directory

Why this threshold: The state directory is full or unwritable.

docs.title: port49_inventory_snapshot_stale
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

The inventory snapshot in force was last confirmed over a day ago, or there is none; the fleet still authenticates on it, and nothing fails closed.

port49_inventory_snapshot_age_seconds > 86400 or port49_inventory_snapshot_age_seconds != port49_inventory_snapshot_age_seconds

Source: A stale inventory snapshot: port49_inventory_snapshot_age_seconds raises an alarm, never a fail-closed

Why this threshold: 86400 is a day; set your sync cadence times a few. The NaN arm (no snapshot yet) is the spec's own expression. Not gated: a process that never watches the inventory reads 0, and one that waits for its first snapshot reads NaN from before its listener opens, which is the case the NaN arm is for.

docs.title: port49_inventory_policy_mismatch
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 5m.

The inventory service built the bundle in force against a policy other than port49d's own; port49d applies the inventory against its own policy.

port49_inventory_policy_mismatch == 1

Source: An inventory bundle built against a policy other than port49d's: the hash mismatch is logged and alarmed

Why this threshold: Five minutes outlasts a policy rollout reaching both.

docs.title: port49_inventory_privilege_changes
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

A source-of-truth edit moved privilege: a device changed key or platform, was admitted or added, gained an address, or entered or left a security_log scope; the inventory_change record names the device.

increase(port49_inventory_changes_total{kind=~"key_ref_changed|platform_changed|admission_changed|address_added|scope_joined|scope_left|device_added"}[1h]) > 0

Source: Source-of-truth edits that move privilege: port49_inventory_changes_total{kind}

Why this threshold: Every kind but transport_changed, which has its own alert. A device_added during onboarding raises it too: expected, and it is the only place a new capture target shows.

docs.title: etcd_no_leader
docs.text:
Severity: page. For: 1m.

An etcd member has no leader; a dark member costs up to 12 s, a lost quorum stops the store.

etcd_server_has_leader == 0

Source: An etcd member with no leader: etcd_server_has_leader == 0

Why this threshold: A minute rides out an election.

docs.title: etcd_db_nearly_full
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

An etcd member's database is over 80% of its quota; at the quota etcd refuses writes.

etcd_mvcc_db_total_size_in_bytes / etcd_server_quota_backend_bytes > 0.8

Source: An etcd database nearly at its quota: etcd_mvcc_db_total_size_in_bytes / etcd_server_quota_backend_bytes > 0.8

Why this threshold: Defragment or compact before the quota: ten minutes is not a spike.

docs.title: etcd_disk_slow
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: 10m.

etcd's disk cannot keep up; port49 store calls will time out in bursts. Move etcd to a disk with sustained fsync p99 under 10 ms (datacenter NVMe or a cloud SSD volume).

histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 0.010 or histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(etcd_disk_backend_commit_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 0.025

Source: An etcd disk too slow, by port49's own threshold: p99 of etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds over 10 ms, or of etcd_disk_backend_commit_duration_seconds over 25 ms

Why this threshold: etcd's own guidance is a WAL fsync p99 under 10 ms; a drive that stalls can push store calls past the 500 ms call timeout in bursts: on a CT1000P3PSSD8 drive the session etcd logged 7974 to 9244 slow applies in cells d and e (tests/lab/results/load-beehive.md), against 1 and 0 in RAM (tests/lab/results/load-beehive-ram.md) and at most 74 on a GCE pd-ssd (operator-declared; a 44, c 74, d 1, e 0) with a WAL fsync mean of 0.72 to 0.86 ms (tests/lab/results/load-p49-gce-n2s16.us-central1-a.c.port49.internal.md). Ten minutes over a 5m rate is a drive, not a compaction.

docs.title: etcd_leader_changes
docs.text:
Severity: ticket. For: none.

etcd changed leader more than 3 times in an hour: a flapping network or a slow disk.

increase(etcd_server_leader_changes_seen_total[1h]) > 3

Source: etcd changing leader too often: increase(etcd_server_leader_changes_seen_total[1h]) > 3

Why this threshold: Occasional changes are rollouts; four in an hour is a fault.

docs.title: Decision log
docs.text:
port49 writes one JSON record for every decision it makes, and each record is one line of the log. The log is port49's own record of what it decided, for whom and against which rule. It is separate from the accounting records a device sends, which report what a device did. Every key is snake_case.

Every record has the same envelope: ts, event and, for a decision, verdict and reason. The blocks that follow (auth, device, session and the rest) appear on the records they apply to. Most fields are left out of a record when they have no value, so a query must treat a missing key as "not set".

A record that names its policy blob can be replayed offline and must give the same verdict. The reason codes page lists every value of reason.

The meanings are the policy-engine spec's own text, so a section or decision number in one points into the spec. A lab ID in a meaning is an entry of the spec's lab register, marked open or closed. It stays open until a lab test has measured the behavior it names, and a claim that cites an open entry is not yet measured.

docs.title: Events
docs.text:
A decision event records one decision, with a verdict and a reason.

Event Emitted by What it decides mint broker which grants matched, which roles composed, which blob resulted. A record a sweep page writes through the mint (POST /v1/tokens by scope) carries sweep: {scope, after}; the revocation re-check's records after the mint do not (§13 decision 42 ruling 4). A record of a device under a per-login requirement carries per_login_mfa: {accept, reuse_for_seconds, levels, method, proved_at, reused} (§5.1.5) redeem daemon whether a presented credential is valid, and creates the context authorize_session daemon the session and its returned attributes (§6) authorize_command daemon one command vector escalate daemon an enable exchange, attributed to the principal (§7) refresh broker whether a live context takes the policy now in force, or is revoked (§5.1.3); or, on a session refresh (/v1/refresh), whether it is extended, with session.auth_time and session.session_expires (§5.6); or, on a policy refresh, session.session_expires where the ceiling moved earlier. A context on a platform that never asks about a command carries session.unreached: true (decision 21). On a session refresh, a context under a requirement no proof covers is deny per_login_mfa_required, not extended (§5.1.5). A refresh record under a requirement carries per_login_mfa: {…} as the mint's does revoke broker a revocation by principal or by certificate (§5.1.4): what it reached, and the live contexts it could not; a revocation lifted; or, over HTTP, a principal ending its own sessions (by: self) or a (device, username) key ended (by: key), neither leaving a mark identity broker what GET /v1/identity resolved the caller to: permit grants_matched when its subject holds a grant unexpired now, else deny no_grants_matched (design document §17) explain broker a hypothetical decision POST /v1/explain answered, about the caller or, under explain_others, another principal: its verdict and reason are the answer given, or deny api_right_missing. It authorizes nothing, and replay passes over it issue broker whether a person's sign-in is exchanged for a port49-issued certificate: an OIDC sign-in at POST /v1/certificate (§13 decision 43 ruling 8), or a directory-password sign-in at POST /v1/sign-in or /v1/sign-in/confirm (§13 decision 47): permit certificate_issued, carrying certificate: {serial, issuer, fingerprint, not_after} and auth.oidc or auth.directory_password: {amr, auth_time, entry_sha256}, or a deny with the refusal's reason. A directory sign-in's record carries sign_in: {source}, and on a deny failed (name, second_factor, second_factor_skew, password, directory_state, enrollment, principal_limit, source_limit) with skew_seconds, directory_result and directory_data where they apply. It never carries the name typed, the password, the code or the secret. A broker that cannot issue (issuance_unavailable) records nothing per_login_mfa broker whether a per-login proof posted to POST /v1/mfa is accepted (§5.1.5; §13 decision 45): permit per_login_mfa_proved or deny per_login_mfa_refused, carrying per_login_mfa: {method, challenge_sha256}. A proof the broker cannot judge (store_unavailable) records that admin_touch broker an admin-level call's proof outcome (§5.1.6; §13 decision 54 ruling 15): deny admin_touch_required (a challenge was issued, nothing done), permit admin_touch_proved (the operation's own record follows), deny admin_touch_refused or deny admin_touch_unavailable, carrying admin: {operation, target, challenge_sha256, why}, where why is on a refusal or an unavailable answer one of a closed set of fixed words and never text from the request: no_roots, bearer, no_client_certificate, no_exporter, malformed_proof, unknown_challenge, touch_slot_chain, session_slot_chain, device_mismatch, touch_policy, session_key, bad_signature. A record never carries the challenge, the signature, the attestations or the exporter value; the cause text is in the API answer alone enroll broker whether a person's TOTP second factor is enrolled (POST /v1/sign-in/confirm; §13 decision 47 ruling 4): permit second_factor_enrolled, carrying auth.directory_password and sign_in: {source}, or a deny with the sign-in's reasons. Every enrollment is alertable: inside an enrollment window a stolen password enrolls the thief's authenticator blob broker not a decision: the full compiled blob, emitted once per hash so replay depends on the log alone (§5.1.1)

docs.title: Report events
docs.text:
A report event shares the envelope but is not a decision: it carries no verdict.

Event Emitted by What it reports account daemon A device's accounting record: what the device did, after the fact. It carries the record block and no policy block. account_gap daemon Accounting records port49 received and did not write to the log, with the gap block: the stage, how many and since when. A window with a gap cannot say a device did not ask. unvalidated daemon A packet no key validated, or a connection the listener refused or ended: the unvalidated block, with a diagnosis, the cleartext header fields and a hash of the body. Never the body. inventory_change daemon and broker One security-relevant change a policy or inventory swap made, in the change block, with the device in the device block. port49_inventory_changes_total{kind} counts them. directory_forget broker An operator ran port49 directory forget for a principal, which deleted the principal's directory membership and the entry it was pinned to. The forget block holds the entry. second_factor_reset broker An operator reset a person's second factor (port49 directory reset-second-factor), or port49-broker init-enrollments created the enrollment store. The second_factor_reset block holds the cleared enrollment. sign_in_unlock broker An operator cleared a principal's failed-attempt count (port49 directory unlock). The sign_in_unlock block holds the count the broker held. enrollments_import broker An operator ran port49 directory import, which filled or replaced the enrollment store. The enrollments_import block holds the record count and the export time. generic_platform daemon port49d serves an admitted device whose platform has no adapter, with the set's generic adapter. One record per such device at start and at each bundle swap. It carries no verdict, and the broker does not write it.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Type Description ts timestamp When the record was written, as an RFC 3339 timestamp. event string What the record is about. The two events tables list each value: the decision events and what they decide, then the report events. verdict string permit or deny. Absent on the report events, which decide nothing, and on an explain that answered with a mint error. reason string Why the verdict is what it is: one value of the closed reason vocabulary. principal string Who the decision was about. auth.method string How the caller authenticated. auth.credential_sha256 string The SHA-256 of the credential presented on the wire. The credential itself is never logged. A mint record has no value here and carries mint.token_sha256 for each token it issued. auth.fingerprint string The SHA-256 of a client certificate that the trust anchor verified and the broker then refused. It says whose certificate it was. Identity, not a secret. auth.directory.source string Where the directory membership this decision used came from: fresh (read from a server for this request) or grace (the stored membership, still inside the grace period). auth.directory.verified_at string When the membership was last verified against the directory. auth.directory.server string The directory server the membership was read from. auth.directory.site string The directory site the membership was read from. auth.oidc.issuer string The issuer of the verified OIDC token. auth.oidc.sub string The subject of the verified OIDC token. auth.oidc.sid string The identity provider's own session id, when the token carries one. auth.oidc.amr list of string The token's authentication methods references. Recorded because how someone authenticated cannot be established afterwards. No decision reads it. auth.oidc.acr string The token's authentication context class reference. Recorded and read by nothing. auth.oidc.auth_time string When the identity provider says the person authenticated. auth.k8s.cluster string The configured name of the cluster whose verifier accepted the service account token. auth.k8s.issuer string The issuer of the verified service account token. auth.k8s.sub string The subject of the verified service account token. auth.k8s.serviceaccount_uid string The UID of the service account. auth.k8s.pod string The name of the pod the token was issued to. auth.k8s.pod_uid string The UID of the pod the token was issued to. auth.k8s.node string The node the pod ran on, when the token names one. auth.k8s.jti string The token's id, when it carries one. auth.directory_password.amr list of string The methods a directory-password sign-in used. auth.directory_password.auth_time string When the sign-in authenticated. auth.directory_password.entry_sha256 string A SHA-256 of the directory entry that signed in. Never the password or the code. device.nas string The device's address as port49 saw it. device.name string The device's name in the inventory. device.platform string The device's platform in the inventory. device.key_ref string The key that validated the exchange. Set on every record of a validated exchange and on no other. A record from the TLS listener has none. device.key_version integer The version of that key. port49 keys status reads a rotation's phase-out from it. device.transport string tls on a record from the TACACS+ over TLS (RFC 9887) listener. Absent on the RFC 8907 listener's records. device.cert_sha256 string On a TLS record, the SHA-256 of the device's verified leaf certificate. session.ctx_id string The id of the context (the session state port49 holds for a login). It joins the records of one login. session.username string The username the device sent. Left empty when the device sent a token-shaped username, which the log never carries. session.username_redacted boolean true when the device sent a token-shaped username and it was left out of session.username. session.replaced_ctx_id string On a redeem that replaced an existing context for the same device and username, the id of the displaced context. A second login by the same principal joins the context and sets nothing here. session.replaced_unreadable boolean true when the replaced context could not be opened (sealed under a key that has left the two-key window, or failing authentication), so its id cannot be named. session.revoked_at string On a redeem refused credential_revoked, when the revocation that refused it was made. session.privilege_clamped.from integer The privilege level the context held before a login joined it. session.privilege_clamped.to integer The level it was lowered to, which is the newest login's ceiling. Another window's next command above this level is denied privilege_exceeded. session.auth_time string On a refresh record that moved it, the session's new authentication time. session.session_expires string On a refresh record that moved it, the session's new ceiling; on a redeem refused session_expired, the ceiling that refused it. session.unreached boolean true on a refresh record for a context on a platform that never asks about a command, or on a device whose inventory entry gives no platform. The live session keeps what it had. session.port string The port (tty) the device reported on this exchange. session.rem_addr string The remote address the device reported on this exchange. session.privilege integer On authorize_session and authorize_command, the privilege level in the request's header, which is the level the device asked at. On other events, what that event says: a refresh's is the context's level and a redeem's is the login's start level. session.held_privilege integer The privilege level port49 held for the context when the request arrived, before any raise this request makes. Present on authorize records whose context was read and is this user's, denials included. Compare it with session.privilege to see what the device asked for against what port49 held. request.service string The service attribute of the request. Recorded on every authorize_session and authorize_command record, denials included, so it can be grouped by. It is checked against the platform's session services and nothing else. request.raw list of string The request's arguments as the device sent them, after redaction: a word that matches a secret rule is replaced with «redacted» first, and request.redacted says so. request.vector list of string The request's command as a list of words. request.redacted boolean true when words were replaced with «redacted» before the record was written. A secret is never logged. packet_fields.action string The authentication action, as a name. Authentication requests only. packet_fields.authen_type string The authentication type, as a name. packet_fields.service string The authentication service, as a name. packet_fields.authen_method string The authentication method, as a name. Authorization and accounting requests only. packet_fields.priv_lvl integer The privilege level in the request header. reply.attributes list of string The attributes a permitted authorization returned to the device, as sent, with every placeholder filled. flags string On an account record, the accounting flags the device sent, such as stop. attribution string On an account record, whether the record was tied to a login port49 knows. resolved: it was. foreign: a record for a session whose start port49 never saw, on a device where it did watch this user's other sessions begin (a local fallback, a console login, or a device-local account with the same name); this is the value to alert on, and port49_accounting_attributions_total{attribution="foreign"} counts it. system: the device acting on its own behalf. unattributed: none of these. task_id string The task_id of an accounting record. record.raw list of string On an account record, the accounting arguments as the device sent them, after redaction: a word that matches a secret rule is replaced with «redacted» before the record is written, and record.redacted says so. record.vector list of string On an account record, the command as a list of words. record.redacted boolean true when words were replaced before the accounting record was written, so no secret reaches the disk. record.priv_lvl integer The privilege level in the accounting record. record.start_time integer The device's start time for the task, when it sent one. record.stop_time integer The device's stop time for the task, when it sent one. record.elapsed_time integer The device's elapsed time for the task, when it sent one. mint.token_sha256 list of string The SHA-256 of each token the mint issued. The token itself never appears in the log. mint.ttl_seconds integer How long the minted tokens live, in seconds. mint.blob string The hash of the policy blob the mint resulted in. policy.bundle string The policy version the blob was compiled from. policy.blob string The hash of the compiled blob the decision was made against. With policy.bundle, it is what makes the record replayable. policy.subject string The subject that matched the principal. policy.subjects list of string Every subject that matched, sorted, when the principal matches more than one. policy.subject is then absent. policy.grants.[].scope string On a mint record, the scope of a grant that selected the device. policy.grants.[].roles list of string The roles that grant gives. policy.grants.[].expires string When the grant stops matching. Empty means never. policy.matched_deny.rule list of string The rule's terms as written. policy.matched_deny.specificity list of integer The specificity tuple the rule scored against this command. policy.matched_deny.role string The role that carries the rule. The rule is the deny that decided a no_permit_dominates_deny, or the most specific deny a permit overrode. policy.matched_permits.[].rule list of string The rule's terms as written. policy.matched_permits.[].specificity list of integer The specificity tuple the rule scored against this command. policy.matched_permits.[].role string The role that carries the rule. The permits that matched the command are listed most specific first, and the first decided a permit. policy.stage integer The 1-based pipeline stage that a pipe_stage_denied refused. The stage's words are in request.raw. blob.hash string The hash that names the blob. blob.body object On a blob record, the compiled blob whole, emitted once per hash, so replay depends on the log alone. blob.redacted boolean true when rule text in the body was redacted before it was logged. The body is then not the blob the hash names, and replay reports every record that names it unverifiable. unvalidated.source string The source address of a packet no key validated. unvalidated.diagnosis string Why the packet or connection is on this record. no_known_key_matches: no key of the device's key_ref validates it. matches_retired: a retired key validates it, and unvalidated.version says which. unencrypted_refused: the packet was not obfuscated. not_tacacs: the header is not TACACS+. unadmitted_source: the source address is not in the inventory. malformed_after_validation: the key validated and the body did not decode. device_quarantined: the device is admitted but quarantined by policy. admission_refused: the device is in the inventory and admission refused it. admission_withdrawn: a reload renamed, re-keyed or re-platformed the device of an open connection. transport_mismatch: the device reached the listener it does not speak. tls_refused: the TLS listener refused or ended the connection, and unvalidated.tls_outcome says why. obfuscated_over_tls: a packet over TLS with the unencrypted flag clear. unvalidated.key_ref string The key tried, when there was one. unvalidated.version integer The version of the key (the numbered version within the device's key_ref) that the packet matched, or that the connection speaks. During a key rotation, a matches_retired record carries the retired version a device is still using, which is how you find the devices that have not moved to the new key. Absent where no key matched. unvalidated.type integer The packet type in the header. unvalidated.seq_no integer The sequence number in the header. unvalidated.session_id integer The session id in the header. unvalidated.length integer The body length in the header. unvalidated.body_sha256 string The SHA-256 of the body. The body itself is never logged. unvalidated.transport string tls on a record from the TLS listener. unvalidated.tls_outcome string On a record with diagnosis: tls_refused, why the handshake was refused. See the values below. unvalidated.detail string A bounded, printable note on a record from the TLS listener, or on a transport_mismatch record from either listener (which names the transport the device record says and the listener it reached). It is never a body. unvalidated.cert_sha256 string On a record with diagnosis: tls_refused, the SHA-256 of the certificate the device sent, where it sent one. server_msg string The message the reply carried to the person at the device. A denial's names the rule that decided and does not echo the command. gap.stage string Where accounting records were dropped: offer_refused (answered ERROR, so the device may send the record again), drain_unparseable or drain_set_aside (answered SUCCESS and not in the log). gap.records integer How many accounting records were dropped at this stage. gap.since string The earliest arrival among the dropped records, as far as the spool knows it. change.kind string What changed. Only security-relevant changes are written: device_added (a device added and admitted), admission_changed (a device already in the inventory becoming admitted), address_added (an address added to a device already in the inventory), key_ref_changed, transport_changed and platform_changed (a device's key assignment, transport or platform changed), and scope_joined or scope_left (a device entering or leaving a scope with security_log: true). change.scope string The scope involved, when the change names one. change.address string The address involved, when the change names one. change.from string The earlier value, on key_ref_changed, transport_changed, platform_changed and admission_changed. change.to string The later value, on those kinds and on device_added, where it is admitted. change.from_bundle string The policy version before the swap that made the change. change.to_bundle string The policy version after it. forget.entry_id string The id of the directory entry the principal was pinned to. forget.dn string The distinguished name of that entry. forget.verified_at string When the entry was last verified or refused. forget.refused boolean true when the last answer for the entry was a refusal. forget.origin string Who asked for the principal to be forgotten. sweep.scope string On a mint record made through a sweep page, the scope the sweep walked. sweep.after string The page's cursor. revocation.by string What the revocation was made by, such as a principal or a certificate. revocation.issuer string The issuer of a certificate revoked by serial. revocation.serial string The serial of a certificate revoked by serial. revocation.oidc_issuer string The OIDC issuer of a session or subject ended by a back-channel logout or a revocation by sid or sub. revocation.sid string The OIDC session id that was ended. revocation.sub string The OIDC subject that was ended. revocation.principals list of string Every principal a logout reached, when its owner record named more than one. The record's principal is then the first. revocation.device string The device a revocation was limited to. revocation.username string The username a revocation was limited to. revocation.at string When the revocation was made. revocation.origin string Who made the revocation. revocation.contexts integer How many live contexts it reached. Zero is left out. revocation.token_keys integer How many token keys it reached. Zero is left out. revocation.connections integer How many connections it ended. Zero is left out. revocation.unreached.[].device string A live context the revocation could not reach: its device. revocation.unreached.[].username string A live context the revocation could not reach: its username. revocation.saved boolean Whether broker.revocations_file was written. Present for a standing mark only: absent for a self or key revocation, which writes none, and on a broker that keeps no revocations_file. revocation.error string What went wrong, when something did. explain.asked_by string The principal that asked the hypothetical question. explain.asked_by_fingerprint string The fingerprint of the certificate the asker presented. explain.command boolean true when the question was about a command. The command itself is never recorded. explain.mint_error string The mint error the broker would have answered instead of a token. The record then has no verdict. certificate.serial string The serial of the certificate issued, as port49 revoke --cert-serial takes it. certificate.issuer string The distinguished name of the CA that issued it. certificate.fingerprint string Its SHA-256 fingerprint. certificate.not_after string When it expires. per_login_mfa.accept list of string On a mint or refresh record under a per-login requirement, the proof methods the requirement accepts. per_login_mfa.reuse_for_seconds integer How long a proof is reused for, in seconds. per_login_mfa.levels list of string The privilege levels the requirement covers. per_login_mfa.method string The method of the proof that covered the record, or of the proof a per_login_mfa record judged. per_login_mfa.proved_at string When the covering proof was made. per_login_mfa.reused boolean true when an earlier proof was reused. per_login_mfa.challenge_sha256 string On a per_login_mfa record, the SHA-256 of the challenge. The challenge itself is never logged. admin.operation string On an admin_touch record, the operation the proof was for. admin.target string The operation's target, as the challenge shows it. admin.challenge_sha256 string The SHA-256 of the challenge. The challenge, the signature and the attestation are never logged. admin.why string For a refusal or an unavailable answer, a fixed cause. sign_in.source string The source network a directory-password sign-in came from. sign_in.failed string On a refusal, which check failed. sign_in.skew_seconds integer For a clock too far off, by how many seconds. sign_in.directory_result integer The directory's result code, on a refusal that has one. sign_in.directory_data string The directory's diagnostic data, on a refusal that has one. Never the name typed, the password or the code. second_factor_reset.enrolled_at string When the enrollment that was cleared was made. second_factor_reset.enrolled_from string Where it was made from. second_factor_reset.reopen_until string Until when enrollment is open again. Absent on a store creation. second_factor_reset.all boolean true for a reset of every enrollment. second_factor_reset.created boolean true when the record is the creation of the enrollment store. second_factor_reset.origin string Who made the reset. sign_in_unlock.failures integer The failed-attempt count the answering broker held. Absent when its session store did not answer the clear: the unlock is then in force but the count is unknown, which is not zero. sign_in_unlock.origin string Who cleared the count. enrollments_import.records integer How many enrollment records the import wrote. enrollments_import.exported_at string When the imported export was made. enrollments_import.replaced boolean true when the import replaced an existing store. enrollments_import.origin string Who ran the import. index_error string What a failed session-index write cost, on the record for the session that lost it. That session is missing from the index, so a later revocation cannot find it. This is different from revocation.unreached, which lists live contexts a revocation found and could not reach.

docs.title: The tls_outcome values
docs.text:
A record from the RFC 9887 (TACACS+ over TLS) listener carries transport: "tls". An unvalidated record with diagnosis: tls_refused carries the tls_outcome that says why the handshake was refused. The handshake counter port49_tls_handshakes_total uses the same values as its outcome label. Strike says whether the refusal counts against the source address, as a wrong key does.

tls_outcome Means Strike version_refused The ClientHello offered no TLS 1.3. yes no_client_certificate The device sent no certificate. yes unknown_ca Its chain reaches no client_ca_file anchor. yes certificate_expired A certificate in its chain is expired or not yet valid. yes certificate_invalid Any other path error, a serverAuth-only leaf included. yes certificate_revoked A certificate in its chain is revoked. yes status_unavailable Its status could not be established under on_unavailable: refuse. A decline: the window stands until it lapses. no identity_mismatch The leaf does not name the device its source address is. yes sni_mismatch The ClientHello asked for a server name not in server_names. A decline: the window stands until it lapses. no early_data_refused The ClientHello carried early_data (RFC 9887 section 5.1.2). yes handshake_timeout No handshake within handshake_timeout. yes handshake_failed Anything else: a bad signature, a client abort. yes

Two more values are never in a record. They are label values of port49_tls_handshakes_total only, and both mean the device was admitted:

  • ok: The handshake completed and the device's certificate was admitted. Counted after the status check passes.
  • resumed: The handshake resumed an earlier TLS session and the device was admitted.

docs.title: packet_fields
docs.text: A record for a validated request carries packet_fields: the request's header fields as names, not numbers. These are action (authentication only), authen_type, service, authen_method (authorization and accounting only) and priv_lvl. A value outside the protocol's list is written unknown_<n>, where <n> is the header byte. A record for an unvalidated packet has no packet_fields; it has the unvalidated block, which holds only cleartext header fields.

docs.title: What the log never holds
docs.text: The log never contains a token, a password, a challenge or a response. A credential appears only as credential_sha256. The body of an unvalidated packet is never logged, only its hash. A token typed as a username leaves session.username empty and sets session.username_redacted to true.

docs.title: Lab register
docs.text:
Every page of this site that says how a device behaves rests on a claim that port49's lab can test. Each claim has an ID, an L-number such as the ones linked throughout the site, and this page lists them all. A claim is one question about a device or a protocol, for example whether a switch shows a message port49 sends with a denial, and the lab answers it on real device images.

  • Open means the lab has not finished measuring the claim. The documentation never asserts an open claim as fact: where a page mentions one, it says the behavior is unmeasured, or it cites the results note for the platform it measured. A row can be open while one platform is measured and others are not.
  • Closed means a lab test passed and a results note records the platform, the image version, what was observed and where the capture is. The note is the evidence.

A results note wins over any page: when a note and a page disagree, the page is wrong and is corrected to match the note. The register itself is section 15 of the policy-engine spec, and the rows below are shortened from it. Follow the spec link for a row's full wording.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Every metric port49d and port49-broker export on /metrics, with its type, labels and help text. The list is read from the registered collectors. Each section holds the series whose names share a second word, such as accounting in port49_accounting_spool_depth. No metric carries a device's identity as a label. The last column links each shipped alert whose expression uses the series.

docs.title: accounting
docs.text: Metric Type Labels Meaning Alerts port49_accounting_attributions_total counter attribution Accounting records accepted, by attribution. port49_accounting_foreign port49_accounting_spool_depth gauge Accounting records waiting for the sink. port49_accounting_spool_drops_total counter stage Accounting records discarded by the spool, by the stage that discarded them. port49_accounting_spool_drops port49_accounting_spool_quarantines_total counter Unreadable spool files renamed aside for an operator. port49_accounting_spool_sync_seconds histogram Seconds one accounting spool group commit spent in fsync and close (plus the directory fsync of a new file); every record in the batch waits on it. port49_accounting_spool_disk_slow

docs.title: Reason codes
docs.text:
The reason of a decision record is one of the codes below, and nothing else. The list is closed, so a denial can be counted and alerted on without parsing prose. The metrics use the same codes. The codes are in the order the server declares them.

The meanings are the policy-engine spec's own text, so a section or decision number in one points into the spec. A lab ID in a meaning is an entry of the spec's lab register, marked open or closed. It stays open until a lab test has measured the behavior it names, and a claim that cites an open entry is not yet measured.
