Reason Meaning grants_matched mint: at least one declared grant selected the device; blob written. refresh: the policy in force was written into the live context; or, on a session refresh, the context was extended. identity: the caller's subject holds a grant unexpired now no_grants_matched mint: no declared grant for this principal selects the device; or, on a sweep page by scope, the page holds no device: the scope is not declared, selects no device the principal holds a grant on, or the page is past the end, which are one answer and one record carrying sweep and policy.bundle and no device (§13 decision 42 ruling 2), after the mint gate has passed. refresh: none does any more, and the live context is revoked. identity: it holds none username_collision mint: the derived username is already held by a subject in another trust domain (§2); or the directory derives a username a policy subject declares (the declared one stands, whichever came first; §13 decision 38 ruling 3, decision 40 ruling 6), or a second directory entry holds the same username under broker.directory.username_attribute (§13 decision 38); or a workload under a directory mapping whose identity subject declares no username takes from its entry one a subject declares or a second entry holds (§13 decision 41 ruling 4, plan 8b). At the broker's bind and on refresh likewise; on refresh every context of the principal is revoked. The process log names both claimants trust_domain_unresolved mint: no configured verifier accepted the credential (design document §7); or the revocation status of the certificate or one above it could not be established (a stale CRL, an OCSP responder that did not answer, an issuer no configured source covers, which is final at port49 workload, §13 decision 40 ruling 7) and broker.certificate_status.on_unavailable is refuse (§5.1.4). The API then answers 503 certificate_status_unavailable, never a final 401, and to be retried but for an uncovered issuer. A certificate whose verified chains end at both the human and the workload trust anchor, or, on a broker with no human x509 verifier, do not end at the workload anchor (§13 decision 40 ruling 2), is refused at the TLS handshake, which leaves a log line and a handshake_failures{identity_refused} count, not a decision record. On mint, refresh, identity, explain, revoke and issue also: an OIDC token none of broker.identity's verifiers accepts, or that two accept (a bad signature, an algorithm the verifier does not pin, an iss, aud or azp that does not match, an expired or not-yet-valid token, one issued longer ago than max_token_age, a human token without auth_time, a machine token from a client the verifier does not list, with another sub than the client's, or carrying a person's session claim or an idtyp other than app) (§13 decision 39); or a Kubernetes service account token the cluster's k8s verifier does not accept: a bad signature, an algorithm it does not pin, an iss it does not name, an aud other than exactly its audience, a token expired, not yet valid, ahead of the broker's clock or older than max_token_age, a typ other than JWT, a person's session claim, or a token not bound to a pod (no kubernetes.io claim, its namespace or service account not the sub's, no pod, or a secret binding) (§13 decision 49 rulings 5–7); the API answers a final 401, never certificate_status_unavailable. When the issuer's keys cannot be had (none fetched, none refreshed within jwks_max_age, or a token's kid not in the kept set and the refetch failing) the API answers 503 identity_provider_unavailable, to be retried, never a final 401. On refresh: the refresh challenge was not answered by the connection's key, or the certificate's status could not be established as on mint (503); also an OIDC refresh whose token's nonce is not the caller's unspent challenge (401 refresh_challenge_missing), or whose auth_time is before it (401 refresh_not_fresh). On issue: a missing bearer, a client certificate presented, a sign-in older than the freshness bound, a nonce not naming the CSR's key, a spent sign-in, a bad CSR, a machine token, or a sign-in that cannot be carried in a certificate (§13 decision 43 ruling 8) candidate_cap_reached mint: token.candidate_cap unspent tokens already stand for this (device, username); the mint is refused, never a redemption, and every token already issued stays usable (design document §8). A mint whose reply is lost after its commit leaves a token nobody holds; it counts toward the cap until it expires (at most 15 minutes, the longest token_ttl) identity_unmapped at the broker's bind, and on mint, identity, explain, revoke and issue: an OIDC token that verified but whose principal claim is absent, not one string, not printable ASCII with an @, outside the verifier's principal_domains, or an email without email_verified: true, or a machine token with neither azp nor client_id (§13 decision 39); or a Kubernetes service account token that verified but whose sub is not system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<name> in the form §2 gives, or whose namespace the cluster's k8s verifier does not list in namespaces (§13 decision 49 ruling 8); or the client certificate maps to no directory entry under broker.directory.certificate_mapping; or the value the mapping reads is not in the certificate (no SID extension; zero or several UPN or email SANs); or a weak mapping's issuer is not one its issuers: pins (design §7); or a certificate the workload anchor verified names no workload: zero or several URI SANs, a URI that is not a SPIFFE ID with a path, a trust domain outside broker.identity.machines[].spiffe_trust_domains, or a leaf that is a CA (§13 decision 40), answered 401 at bind over HTTP, never as a TLS alert; or, under a workload certificate's directory mapping (§13 decision 41, plan 8b), its issuer is not one broker.identity.machines[].directory.issuers pins, no entry under base_dn holds its SPIFFE ID in the mapping's attribute, or the entry found holds that attribute with other than one value equal to the SPIFFE ID byte for byte; or, while that mapping is configured, a person's entry holds in the mapping's attribute any value beginning spiffe://, so it is a workload's (§13 decision 41 ruling 4); or the entry's principal_attribute or username_attribute is absent, has several values, is not printable ASCII, gives a principal with no @, or a username that is not already canonical or is reserved (§2); or the principal it gives is pinned to another entry, by objectGUID or entryUUID (else DN), for as long as that principal's membership record lives or until an operator runs port49 directory forget (§13 decision 38). The API answers 401 and the connection is closed. On refresh: the principal's entry is gone or no longer usable, and every context of it is revoked identity_ambiguous as identity_unmapped, when the certificate maps to two or more entries, or the server refuses the search for its size limit; or when a second entry holds the same broker.directory.principal_attribute value as the mapped entry, so two people would share one principal (§13 decision 38); or when two entries hold a workload's SPIFFE ID in the workload mapping's attribute (§13 decision 41, plan 8b); or when a uniqueness search (the username's, the principal's) does not return the entry itself, so the server's matching rule cannot prove the value is one entry's alone; or, on issue and enroll, when a directory sign-in's name matches two entries (§13 decision 47 ruling 9). Never resolved to the first entry (design §7). MUST be alertable on its own: two entries matching one identity is an impersonation path. On refresh: every context of the principal is revoked directory_unavailable at the broker's bind, and on mint, identity, explain and revoke: no directory server answered within broker.directory.query_timeout, and the membership the store holds for the principal or the certificate was verified longer ago than broker.directory.grace, or there is none, or it records the directory's refusal (grace never overrules one) (§13 decision 38); for a workload under a directory mapping, the membership stored for its SPIFFE ID (§13 decision 41 ruling 7, plan 8b), which port49 workload retries within --deadline and then exits 75. Nothing is minted. The API answers 503 with Retry-After, to be retried, and no agent session is ended. Never on a scheduled or policy refresh: a principal the directory does not answer for keeps its contexts unstamped, and context_stale takes over at the ceiling. On a session refresh (/v1/refresh), as on mint: nothing is extended. On issue and enroll, a directory-password sign-in (§13 decision 47): no server answered the entry's search or the person's bind, or the broker's own search was refused (a bind account's rights or a base_dn put wrong: the log holds the LDAP result code); no grace applies, since a password is never kept, so the sign-in is refused 503 at once (design §12) composition_refused mint: the principal matches more than one subject, and their grants together compose on this device to a session reply a joint check refuses (§10): a level above the grants' ceiling, a reply over 255 bytes, an attribute the platform does not accept, or a blob the daemon would refuse. Refused for this principal on this device alone, never a quarantine. On refresh: the live context is revoked the same way. The process log names the subjects and the check token_redeemed redeem: a presented credential matched an unspent token token_not_found redeem: the device tag matched but no unspent token for (nas, username) did — expired, spent, or mistyped, or its receipt deleted by an operator's revocation (§5.1.4) token_spent redeem/escalate: the credential matched a receipt whose sliding window (receipt_idle_ttl) or absolute cap (receipt_max_age) had passed, or whose ctx_id is no longer the live context's — the context was replaced or reclaimed since, so the stored decision describes nothing that exists (§5.6); or, on redeem or escalate, the token's store revision is at or below port49d's restore floor: an etcd restore brought it back (decision 56 ruling 1); FAIL on the wire, distinguishable only in the log device_mismatch redeem: the presented token's device tag is not this device's (design document §8) — PAP and ASCII only; under CHAP the tag is not visible and the outcome is token_not_found credential_mismatch redeem: the receipt the store returned does not carry the credential hash the lookup asked for. Since 2026-09-20 the hash is in the receipt key (§13, decision 15), so a differing credential finds no receipt and redeems normally instead; on redeem this reason now covers only a store that answered with a record it was not asked for, which is a store fault and never a normal outcome. On escalate it also covers an enable token whose principal is not the escalated context's (decision 56 ruling 11); that is a wrong or stolen credential, not a store fault, and the operator should not look at etcd for it receipt_replayed redeem: a byte-identical retransmission replayed the stored decision; not while the context it names is revoked — that is credential_revoked (§5.6). A login refused after its join replays as FAIL once the revocation is lifted token_kind_mismatch redeem/escalate: a login token presented at enable, or the reverse (§7) store_unavailable any event: the store did not answer or returned an error, or, on redeem or escalate on etcd, port49d's last read of meta/witness failed, so it cannot tell whether the store was restored (port49_redemption_restore_unjudged; decision 56 ruling 1), or, on mint at port49-broker, the mint gate is closed (port49_broker_mint_gate_closed): the replica's mark on meta/judged has not landed since its policy swap (one store round trip), or, since its start, the replica has seen no takeover done for the bundle it serves, neither its own runner's nor one meta/judged records, not in doubt (up to hold_ttl/3 and the takeover on a first start or a start after a policy edit, plus up to hold_ttl when the previous run's lease must expire first, as after a crash; none on a rolling restart; decision 36, the purge at a takeover). This is the start gate and not a store fault, and an operator should not look at etcd for it. Its 503 carries Retry-After. port49 workload retries it; the agent does not. port49 token retries a mint refused store_unavailable, waiting the reply's Retry-After (5s when it carries none) between tries, for up to 30s in all, then exits with the same code and its retry wording; it retries no other reason (owner's ruling 2026-10-15, issue #11), so a broker restart's start gate does not fail a script. On redeem and on accounting the reply is ERROR; on an authorization it is FAIL — fail closed, a break-glass account's commands included (plan 4, owner's ruling 2026-09-24), because an authorization ERROR hands the N9Kv's command to its local role checks and permits every command under IOS-XE's if-authenticated (§15, L4 (open)). Whether the device then falls through to its next method is per platform and is not what this reason promises: an authentication ERROR is final on IOS-XE and on Junos with tacplus alone, and where it does fall through (vEOS, the N9Kv) the authorization FAIL that follows leaves break-glass logged in and unable to run a command (§15, L4 (open); tests/lab/results/L4-error-*.md). So a store outage is not the break-glass case; an unreachable port49 is. The operator's escape is to stop port49d, or reject TCP 49 with a reset, so each device finds the connection refused and treats the server as down. A break-glass account then logs in with its local password, under a method list that ends in local (measured over SSH on all five images, §15 L4 (open) and L17 (open)). A firewall that drops TCP 49 silently is unmeasured as an escape (a silent server costs 5s per command on the Cisco and Arista images, L4 (open)), and so is whether commands in a session already open fall to local authorization. port49d does this itself while the store is unhealthy (owner's ruling 2026-09-24; plan 7f). On etcd it checks the store every stores.session.etcd.health.interval (or stores.directory.… when stores.session is omitted), and after close_after consecutive failed checks it closes every listener and resets held connections, idle or loaded. It is dark within close_after × interval + call_timeout of the store stopping: 5.5s at the defaults, measured at 4.8–5.5s on five images (§15 L41 (closed), tests/lab/results/L41-*.md). It opens the listeners again after open_after consecutive checks pass (§13, decision 37). Losing its hold on the store, or a token or context pool's circuit staying open or every call on one being refused for hold_ttl, remains the backstop (decision 35). Before dark, a store that does not answer, or a pool's open circuit, is answered within stores.session.packet_deadline, never left for the device to time out (what each image does then: §15 L35 (closed)). The log line is the evidence an operator needs at 3am context_matched authorize_session: context found, attributes returned escalation_granted escalate: the level was within max_privilege and the mechanism succeeded permit_dominates a permit dominated every matching deny (§5.4) pipe_stage_denied a pipeline stage matched no pipe permit (§4) service_unsupported the authorization service is not one the platform authorizes; on redeem, the authentication action or type is not one port49 serves (only login with ASCII, PAP, or CHAP) and the reply is ERROR enable_refused escalate: the subject's mechanism is none ceiling_exceeded escalate: the requested level is above max_privilege no_rule_matched nothing matched; deny by default. Also a request that is not a session authorization (§5.2) yet names no command, such as cmd= with a cmd-arg no_permit_dominates_deny a deny matched and no permit dominated it context_missing no login context for (nas, username) — port49 did not authenticate this session under that name username_mismatch the request's username differs from the one bound at redemption (§5.6). Reachable two ways, and a request under a name port49 never authenticated is neither of them — that is context_missing, because the username is the key. First, wherever the username is resolved from context rather than read off the wire: the $enab{level}$ enable path through the (nas, rem_addr) index. Second, as a store-fault guard — the context lookup selects on the username, so a store answering with another principal's record fails the re-check that follows it and is denied rather than authorized. A correct store never produces the second rem_addr_mismatch enable arrived from a different address than the bound one privilege_exceeded a command authorization's request level (session.privilege) is above the session's held level (session.held_privilege); session authorization is never denied this (§5.2) session_expired the session ceiling was reached; context retained through the grace window (§5.6). On mint: the held connection's authentication is older than session.max_session_age_default; on every endpoint but the refresh's challenge and refresh, an OIDC token's auth_time is; either way the caller must authenticate again (§13, decision 17). Per item on mint: the device's ceiling (the least max_session_age of its roles, §5.6) has passed since the connection authenticated; run port49 refresh. On refresh: the context is past its grace window and is not extended. On redeem: the token's ceiling has passed; the login is refused FAIL, the token is not spent, and no context is written (§5.6). context_stale the broker has been unreachable past staleness_ceiling, or the principal's directory membership has not been verified for that long (§5.1.3); context retained, denies until refreshed (§5.1.1, design document §9) credential_revoked the context's revoked_at is set — CRL, OCSP, back-channel logout, every grant on the device withdrawn, a subject's username changed, the principal's directory entry gone, ambiguous or renamed to a username another holds, their subjects' composition refused, the policy in force not compiling for the context, or a refresh finding a context it could not open, where the refresh record before it says which (§5.1.3, §5.6); on redeem, a login whose resulting context is revoked because its token was not minted after the revocation, or a retransmission answered while the context it names is revoked (§5.6); on mint, a revocation by principal or by this certificate stands (§5.1.4), or an OIDC logout refuses the token's session or subject, or a CRL or OCSP response names the certificate or an intermediate above it, so nothing is minted and a held connection is closed; on identity, explain and revoke, an OIDC logout refuses the caller's token; on refresh, the caller's certificate is marked, or an OIDC logout refuses the caller's token, or a CRL or OCSP response names it or an intermediate above it, so nothing is extended; on issue, a mark on the principal or an OIDC logout refuses the sign-in's token, so nothing is issued; on revoke, a revocation's own record device_unknown the source address is not in the admission trie (§10). On an unvalidated record: a reload refused, removed, renamed, re-keyed or re-platformed the device an open connection was admitted as, so that admission is no longer one port49d knows, and the connection is reset with no strike (§10, "How a daemon refreshes its snapshot"). On mint and refresh: the device is in inventory and admission refuses it — no key group admits it, two tie on it, or its key_ref is one port49d holds no key for (§10) — so no token is minted for it and its live contexts are revoked: it cannot reach port49d, and a token for it would only be a login that falls to the device's local method (tests/lab/results/quarantine-*.md). As with a quarantine, a subject with no grant on the device is answered no_grants_matched first, so the API tells no caller which devices exist platform_unknown generic_platform: the device's platform has no adapter; generic fallback applied. Written by port49d once per device per bundle (§8); never the reason of a decision blob_unavailable the referenced blob could not be resolved from the store or any cache — a store fault, alarmed (§5.1.1) — or the context no longer fits the blob: a session attribute filled from it exceeds 255 bytes, or a filled-in value carries a separator (=, *) or a control character, either of which the broker refused at mint (§6), or the reply would send a priv-lvl above the context's max_privilege, a priv-lvl that is not a level 0 to 15, or an attribute the blob's accepted_attributes does not take — compositions the load quarantines (§6, §7). On refresh: the policy in force could not be resolved or compiled for this context — an unexpected broker fault, since the reload's load (§5.1.3 step 1) compiled every subject on every device, and what failed quarantined its device or refused the policy under the joint check (§10) — so the context is revoked, failing closed; the process log names the ctx_id and the fault, and it is counted failed. Also on refresh: the context could not be opened, failing authentication (one sealed under a key port49 does not hold is left unrevoked and unrecorded, §5.1.3) — so it is revoked through the monotonic revocation mark, the record names the device and the username its key holds and no principal (the owner and ctx_id are sealed, and the index entry that led to it may be stale), and it is counted failed blob_platform_mismatch the context's blob was compiled for a platform other than the one inventory gives the device — inventory changed since the mint, or the broker and the daemon read different inventories. Its dialect and attributes are another platform's, so it is never answered from; operational, alertable beside blob_unavailable device_quarantined the device is in inventory but failed joint validation against policy (§10); the connection is closed without a reply, as for device_unknown, until fixed. On refresh, a deny recorded once per context per policy version (bundle): the live context is left as it was until the quarantine lifts projection_fail_closed authorize_session, a permit: the session on a projected platform (§8) was answered with its composition's fail-closed reply — every command denied but what the projection proved — because the projection cannot tell the device that composition faithfully (§13, decision 26). The blob carries why (fail_closed: refused_shape, configuration_mode, overflow, unwritable, secret_rule, unsound, argument_deny, a deny Junos cannot match because it names an argument, or configuration_deny, a deny of a configuration statement, which deny-commands never reaches; decision 27). Every other subject on the device is answered as before; policy test and policy diff fail on the composition revocation_lifted revoke: an operator lifted a revocation (§5.1.4). Mints by the principal or certificate are made again; a context the revocation marked stays revoked until a login whose token was minted after the revocation joins it (§5.6; §13, decision 15): for a principal's mark, after the lift; for a certificate's, by any of the principal's other certificates at any time api_right_missing revoke, explain: the caller asked to act on another principal's tokens, sessions or decisions, or on a (device, username) whoever holds it, and its subject declares no api: right that unlocks it (§2); also directory_forget, second_factor_reset, sign_in_unlock and enrollments_import, for a call under a right the subject lacks (§5.1.6). The API answers 403 api_right_missing; nothing is done certificate_issued issue: the broker issued a short-lived client certificate for the key the sign-in's nonce names (§13 decision 43 ruling 8) per_login_mfa_required mint: the device's per-login requirement (§5.1.5) applies and no proof covers it; the item carries a challenge, and nothing is minted for it. refresh: a context under a requirement no proof covers is not extended and keeps its ceiling per_login_mfa_proved per_login_mfa: a proof posted to POST /v1/mfa verified (§13 decision 45 rulings 12 and 13) per_login_mfa_refused per_login_mfa: a proof did not verify: a challenge unknown, spent, expired or another caller's; a touch signature not over this connection's exporter value; an attestation that does not chain to the configured roots, is not always-touch, or is not the session key's token's; an ID token for another principal, not fresh, without an accepted amr, not binding the challenge, or spent. The API answers 401 with the cause. An ID token decision 39 itself refuses (its signature, issuer, audience or expiry; an unmapped identity) is recorded under event per_login_mfa with decision 39's own reason (trust_domain_unresolved, identity_unmapped, …), not as this one, and is not counted in port49_per_login_mfa_total: an alert on forged tokens at /v1/mfa watches those reasons per_login_mfa_unavailable mint, refresh: the device's requirement accepts no method this broker can verify now (no hardware_key_touch.attestation_roots_file loaded, no human OIDC verifier). That device alone; alertable: a configuration fault, not a person's admin_touch_required admin_touch: an admin-level call carried no proof; a challenge was issued, nothing done admin_touch_proved admin_touch: the proof verified, and the operation's own record follows admin_touch_refused admin_touch: the proof did not verify (an unknown, spent, expired, or another caller's, connection's or request's challenge; a signature not over this exporter and request; an attestation that does not chain, is not always-touch, or is not the session key's token's), or the caller cannot prove (no client certificate). The API answers 401 with the cause. Alertable on its own, as per_login_mfa_refused is admin_touch_unavailable admin_touch: no attestation roots loaded. The API answers 503. A configuration fault, alertable sign_in_refused issue, enroll: a directory-password sign-in whose name maps to no entry under the verifier's filters or outside its principal_domains, whose code is wrong, replayed or from a clock too far off, whose password the directory refused, whose entry's state the directory refuses (expired, disabled, locked, must change), or whose second factor is another entry's (§13 decision 47). One reason to the caller on purpose, so the API never says whether the name, the password or the code was wrong; the directory's state is said past the code, or before it only when the directory gives that state to the right password alone (§13 decision 47 ruling 7; a locked account's state is never said from a password alone, L67 (closed)). The record's sign_in.failed says which. The API answers 401. Counted against the source, and against the principal once one is known sign_in_throttled issue, enroll: the sign-in's principal or source has had failures_per_principal or failures_per_source failed attempts in the window; nothing was checked (§13 decision 47 D5). The API answers 429 with Retry-After. Alert on a rise: someone is spraying enrollment_closed issue: a person with no second factor, and no enrollment window open for them; the password is not checked (§13 decision 47 D2, ruling 4). It says a name exists and has no second factor, without a bind, which is accepted (ruling 7). An operator's port49 directory reset-second-factor opens one. The API answers 403 enrollment_store_lost issue, enroll: the broker's enrollment store is lost — it has no creation mark (its file or key is missing, a new install not yet initialised by port49-broker init-enrollments included), or its file will not unseal (a lost or rotated seal key, tampering) (§13 decision 47 D7). Password sign-in is refused for everyone, before anything is counted or read; certificates already issued, tokens and IdP sign-in serve. The API answers 503. On a new install the operator runs port49-broker init-enrollments; otherwise restores the file or the etcd snapshot (port49 directory import), or runs port49 directory reset-second-factor --all. Alertable: port49_directory_enrollment_store_ok reads 0 second_factor_enrolled enroll: a person's TOTP second factor was confirmed with its first code (§13 decision 47 ruling 4). A permit; alertable

docs.title: Client configuration reference
docs.text:
config.yaml is the operator's own file, ~/.port49/config.yaml (or the file PORT49_CONFIG names, or --config), laid over the system-wide /etc/port49/config.yaml that the install may ship. Every key is optional, and port49 login takes each key its flags leave out from here. A key in your file replaces the same key in the system file.

Whoever can write these files chooses which broker you trust, so a file, or a directory holding one, that anyone else can write is refused and never read. An unknown key or a second YAML document is refused.

A relative path is resolved from the file's own directory, and ~/ is your home directory (~user is not expanded). A key reference (a value starting pkcs11:, tpm: or secure-enclave:) is carried as written.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Type Description broker string The broker to log in to. broker_ca string The CA file that pins the broker's certificate. Read once, and held to the same ownership rule as the config file. cert string Your certificate file, for method: x509. key string Your private key: a file, or a key reference on a hardware token. method string How port49 login authenticates: x509 (default), oidc (a sign-in at your identity provider, for which the broker issues a certificate) or directory (a sign-in by directory password, name and authenticator code). sign_in_name string The name the directory knows you by, offered at the directory sign-in's name prompt. Default: your login name. oidc_issuer string Which identity provider to sign in at, when the broker lists several. oidc_ca string The CA that issued the identity provider's TLS certificate. Unset means the system roots. oidc_redirect_port integer The loopback port the sign-in returns to, 0 to 65535. 0 picks a free one. broker_crl string Whether the broker's certificate is checked against the revocation lists it names, before anything is sent to it: check (default) refuses a revoked certificate and says when a list cannot be obtained, require refuses in that case too, off checks nothing. touch_key string A key reference on the same token as key, whose touch the agent may use. issued_key_store string Where the key of a certificate the broker issues lives: auto, file, tpm, secure_enclave or pkcs11. issued_key string The key reference for issued_key_store: tpm or pkcs11. It starts with pkcs11:, tpm: or secure-enclave:.

docs.title: Inventory file reference
docs.text:
An inventory file lists the devices port49 serves: their names, platforms, addresses, attributes and the key that admits each. It is one YAML document; an unknown key (a typo such as keyref: for key_ref:) or a second document is refused, so a mistake cannot silently un-pin a device onto a group key.

The key_groups: block is read from the policy file, where key assignment is reviewed. A block here still loads, with a notice, until it is moved; where both files have one, the policy file's wins.

Paths below use [] for an item of a list.

docs.title: devices
docs.text: Key Type Description devices.[].name string The device's name, which policy scopes, tests and the log use. devices.[].platform string The device's platform, lowercase letters, digits and _, matching an adapter in the pinned platform set or one the policy file defines. A platform with no adapter gets the generic one. devices.[].addresses list of string The IP addresses the device's connections come from, as a list. A connection is matched to its device by source address. devices.[].attributes map of string Free key and value pairs, such as site, role and os_version, that scopes match on and key groups can match on. devices.[].key_ref string Pins the device to one key, by name. The key is a name that the policy file's keys: block (or port49d's) defines; it never holds the secret. devices.[].transport string How the device speaks TACACS+: tcp (default), obfuscated under a shared key, or tls, mutual TLS with no shared key. Any other value makes the device refused rather than the file.

docs.title: key_groups
docs.text: Key Type Description key_groups.[].match.cidr string Matches the devices whose address is in this prefix, written without host bits. A group needs cidr or attributes; one with neither is refused. key_groups.[].match.attributes map of string Matches the devices whose attributes equal all of these pairs. key_groups.[].key_ref string The key that devices in the group are admitted under. Required. A key name: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, at most 64, and not the reserved single_device.

docs.title: Policy file reference
docs.text:
The policy file says who may do what on which devices. port49 policy test loads it the way port49d does and runs its tests:.

It is one YAML document. An unknown key, a second document (a --- separator) or a key this build does not read is refused, and the error names the key or the line.

Paths below use [] for an item of a list and <name> for a key you choose. Every table row is a leaf; a key whose value is a block is documented by the keys under it. Durations need a unit, for example 60s.

Rules are written as words: * for one word, ** for any number, and /regex/ or @class for a term. See the policy guide for the grammar. Rules are never quoted in an error: a refusal names the list and the position.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Type Description platform_set string Pins the platform set (the shipped adapters) this policy renders with, for example 1.0.0, so that a binary upgrade never changes what the policy renders. Unset means set 1.0.0. A set the binary does not ship is refused, and the error lists the sets it does ship.

docs.title: defaults
docs.text: Key Type Description defaults.per_login_mfa.accept list of string The proofs that satisfy the requirement: a list of hardware_key_touch, idp_mfa or both, each at most once. Required when per_login_mfa is present; leave the block out for no requirement. defaults.per_login_mfa.reuse_for string How long one proof counts for later logins, a duration from 0m (a proof at every login) to 8h. Default 15m. defaults.per_login_mfa.applies_to_machines boolean Set true to require the proof of machine identities too. Default false.

docs.title: platforms
docs.text: Key Type Description platforms.<name>.supports list of string The capabilities the adapter declares, a list that must include session. Replaces the inherited list. platforms.<name>.privilege map of list of string Per privilege level, the attribute strings the reply carries at that level, for example readonly: ["priv-lvl=1"]. A level may not send an attribute twice. platforms.<name>.ceiling_levels map of integer Per level, the priv-lvl number (0 to 15) the level stands for where the rendering sends no priv-lvl, used for the token's ceiling. platforms.<name>.entity_classes map of list of string Named sets of device entity names, as lists of RE2 patterns, that rules reference as @class. A class name is lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, and a class may not be empty. platforms.<name>.expands_abbreviations boolean Whether the device sends resolved command words. Needed when the platform sends per-command authorization. platforms.<name>.splits_interface_names boolean Whether the device sends an interface name and its index as two arguments. platforms.<name>.pipe_token string The modifier separator, one argument with no whitespace, for example \|. platforms.<name>.pipe_authorized boolean Whether the device sends the part of a command after the pipe for authorization. platforms.<name>.strip_cr boolean Whether commands end in <cr>, which port49 strips before matching. platforms.<name>.shows_server_msg boolean Whether the device displays a denial's server_msg to the operator. platforms.<name>.privilege_attributes list of string The attribute names that carry privilege on this platform. The only names an attributes: placeholder may go in, and the names whose change port49 policy diff gates. platforms.<name>.inert_attributes list of string The attribute names held to carry no privilege. A name may not also be in privilege_attributes, and a name a level renders is refused here. platforms.<name>.accepted_attributes list of string Where set, every attribute name the session reply may carry. A reply with any other, or a priv-lvl the levels do not render, quarantines the device. An empty list is refused: list the names or remove the key. platforms.<name>.role_order map of list of string Per attribute that names a role, its values lowest first, where the lab measured one fencing less than another. A value not listed ranks above every listed one. priv-lvl ranks by its number and may not be listed. platforms.<name>.device_config list of string The device configuration the adapter's renderings depend on, one printable ASCII line per item, printed by port49 platform show. platforms.<name>.enable_username string The username the device sends in an enable exchange. The only accepted value is principal, the operator's own username. $enab{level}$ is refused at load. platforms.<name>.redact.[].match list of string Words that select the command this pattern applies to, * for one word and ** for any number, at most two **. No regex or class. platforms.<name>.redact.[].after string Remove every word after the first word equal to this one. One word. Give after or from, not both. platforms.<name>.redact.[].from integer Remove every word from this position on; the first argument is 1, and 0 is refused. Give from or after, not both. platforms.<name>.verified string Port49's own claim about its lab coverage of a built-in adapter. Refused in a policy file: an adapter written here is unverified. platforms.<name>.unreachable map of list of string Per level, the commands the device refuses in its own parser, as rules. The dead-rule report reads them. platforms.<name>.unreachable_note map of list of string Port49's own record of a block's unreachable rules the set did not measure. Refused in a policy file; write the rules under unreachable. platforms.<name>.fallback map of string Per level, what the device gives a session on its own when port49 cannot answer, as text. Not empty. platforms.<name>.fallback_note map of string Port49's own record of a block's fallback text over the set's. Refused in a policy file; write the text under fallback. platforms.<name>.local_accounts list of string RE2 patterns, each with one capture group (the account's name), that find a device-local account in the device's configuration. Read by port49 devices check-config. platforms.<name>.config_checks.[].match string An RE2 pattern over one configuration line that the device's configuration must not carry. Required. platforms.<name>.config_checks.[].says string What the matching line costs, shown when it is found. Required. platforms.<name>.command_projection string How rules render for a session-only platform. The only value this build renders is junos_regex. Only a platform the pinned set projects may set it; elsewhere it is refused. platforms.<name>.bits map of list of string On a projected platform, each permission bit's reach in rule form. A block may add to a bit's reach. platforms.<name>.carve_outs map of list of string On a projected platform, the commands a bit alone makes available. A block may drop one and never add one. platforms.<name>.bit_delivery string How permission bits travel to the device: user_permissions (as a user-permissions= attribute of the session reply) or local_user_name (as the name of a template user on the device, see local_user_names). Required on a projected platform. platforms.<name>.local_user_names map of string Under bit_delivery: local_user_name, each level's template user on the device, named p49-<name>. Never remote or a platform system user. platforms.<name>.rpc_entry_denies list of string On a projected platform, the denies a reply adds where a wire deny is the only guard beneath a sent bit. Each is words with a trailing **. platforms.<name>.deny_reach_bits list of string On a projected platform, the bits a reply may send where the grant permits a carve-out of the bit. platforms.<name>.replace boolean Set true to discard the shipped adapter of this name and start from the generic adapter. Not with based_on. platforms.<name>.based_on string Start this new platform from another platform of the pinned set. Not for a name the set already ships, and not with replace.

docs.title: privilege_levels
docs.text: Key Type Description privilege_levels.[].name string The level's name. Required and unique. The list must include readonly, operator and admin, which keep that relative order. privilege_levels.[].parent string The level this one renders as where a platform has no rendering for it. Must be declared, and the reserved levels have no parent.

docs.title: scopes
docs.text: Key Type Description scopes.[].name string The scope's name. Required and unique. Grants refer to it. scopes.[].match map of string, list of string or comparison Selects devices by inventory attribute: each key is an attribute (site, role, platform, os_version and so on), each value a string, a list of strings, or a comparison such as {lt: "21.4R3-S5"} or {re: "..."}. Empty selects every device. name takes names only, not a comparison. scopes.[].on_missing string What to do with a device that has no value for a match key: include or exclude. Required on a scope that attaches a deny or carries a grant with a deny, and where per_login_mfa is set. Default exclude. scopes.[].security_log boolean Whether a device joining or leaving the scope is logged as a security record. A scope that delivers a deny is logged unless this is false. scopes.[].attached_roles.humans list of string Roles every human principal gets on the devices in the scope, without a grant. On an include scope only roles with no permit, privilege or attributes are accepted. scopes.[].attached_roles.machines list of string Roles every machine principal gets on the devices in the scope, without a grant. Same limit on an include scope. scopes.[].per_login_mfa.accept list of string The proofs that satisfy the requirement: a list of hardware_key_touch, idp_mfa or both, each at most once. Required when per_login_mfa is present; leave the block out for no requirement. scopes.[].per_login_mfa.reuse_for string How long one proof counts for later logins, a duration from 0m (a proof at every login) to 8h. Default 15m. scopes.[].per_login_mfa.applies_to_machines boolean Set true to require the proof of machine identities too. Default false.

docs.title: roles
docs.text: Key Type Description roles.[].name string The role's name. Required and unique. baseline, reach_deny and rpc_entry are port49's own and refused. roles.[].privilege string The privilege level the role grants. Must be a declared level. roles.[].reason string Free text recorded with the role, for review: why it exists. roles.[].permit list of string Command rules the role permits, as words. ** is any number of words; /regex/ and @class are terms. roles.[].deny list of string Command rules the role denies. A permit wins over a matching deny only when it is more specific than every deny that matches (dominance; see Policy). A class used in a deny may not turn case-insensitivity off. roles.[].pipe.permit list of string Rules for the part of a command after the pipe that the role permits. Present with an empty list means no pipe is allowed. roles.[].attributes map of list of string Per platform (or all), attribute strings added to the reply. The key must be all, a platform port49 ships or one the inventory names. roles.[].max_session_age string How long a session may last, a duration of at least 1m, or never. roles.[].per_login_mfa.accept list of string The proofs that satisfy the requirement: a list of hardware_key_touch, idp_mfa or both, each at most once. Required when per_login_mfa is present; leave the block out for no requirement. roles.[].per_login_mfa.reuse_for string How long one proof counts for later logins, a duration from 0m (a proof at every login) to 8h. Default 15m. roles.[].per_login_mfa.applies_to_machines boolean Set true to require the proof of machine identities too. Default false.

docs.title: subjects
docs.text: Key Type Description subjects.[].name string The subject's name. Required and unique. subjects.[].group string A directory group of people, as a DN or a group name. Give group or identity (or machine_group), exactly one. The usernames come from the directory; do not set username. subjects.[].machine_group string A group of workloads, resolved through the workload mapping. Not with group. Do not set username. subjects.[].identity string or list of string A list of principals: user:<email> (lowercase), a SPIFFE ID, system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<name> or app:<client_id>. Do not mix people and machines in one subject; a principal belongs to one subject. subjects.[].username string The username the device sends, for an identity subject that has no directory to derive it from. Printable ASCII, already canonical (lowercase, no DOMAIN\ prefix, no @suffix), unique across subjects, and never remote, p49-* or a platform system user. subjects.[].enable string How the subject escalates: none (default), auto or token. subjects.[].token_ttl duration How long a device token lives, 30s to 900s. Required on a subject a grant names. subjects.[].api list of string The broker API rights the subject holds, a list from revoke_others, explain_others, lift_revocations, forget_principals, reset_second_factor, unlock_sign_in, import_enrollments, sync, keys_show and replay.

docs.title: grants
docs.text: Key Type Description grants.[].subject string The subject that gets the roles. Must be declared. grants.[].scope string The scope the grant applies in. Must be declared. grants.[].roles list of string The roles granted, at least one, each declared and listed once. Two grants with the same subject, scope and roles are refused: merge them. grants.[].max_privilege string A ceiling on the privilege level a token from this grant may carry. A level some platform numbers. grants.[].expires string When the grant stops matching: a date (2026-12-01, the start of that day, UTC) or an RFC 3339 time. grants.[].attributes map of list of string Per platform (or all), attribute strings the grant adds to the reply.

docs.title: tests
docs.text: Key Type Description tests.[].subject string The subject the test runs as. Give subject or principal, one of the two. tests.[].principal string A principal identity the test runs as, in any form identity takes. tests.[].device string The inventory device the test runs against. Required. tests.[].command string The command to authorize. A test without a command is a session test. tests.[].expect string permit or deny. Required with a command; not allowed on a session test. tests.[].reason string Optional, with a command. The reason code the decision must carry for the test to pass, on a permit or a deny: for example no_grants_matched or permit_dominates. A code that is not on the reason codes page is refused at load. Not allowed on a session test. tests.[].level string Session test: the privilege level the subject must be minted a token at. tests.[].max_privilege string Session test: the ceiling the token must carry, a level or none. tests.[].priv_lvl string Session test: the priv-lvl number (0 to 15) the reply must carry, or none. tests.[].enable string Session test: the enable mode the subject must have, none, auto or token. tests.[].reply list of string Session test: the exact session reply, in order, as a list of attribute strings. An empty list asserts an empty reply. tests.[].api list of string Session test: the broker API rights the subject must hold, in any order. tests.[].per_login_mfa none or mapping Session test: the effective per-login requirement on the device, none or a mapping of accept and reuse_for.

docs.title: acknowledge
docs.text: Key Type Description acknowledge.[].role string Names a deny by its role. Give role and rule together. acknowledge.[].rule string The deny rule as written in the role. It must exist. acknowledge.[].platform string Names an adapter edit by its platform. Give platform, field and sha256 together. acknowledge.[].field string The adapter key the edit changed. acknowledge.[].sha256 string The digest port49 policy diff prints for the key's new value, 64 lowercase hex digits. The entry acknowledges that edit and no later one. acknowledge.[].reason string Why the change is accepted. Required; review reads it beside the change.

docs.title: key_groups
docs.text: Key Type Description key_groups.[].match.name string Matches one device by its inventory name. A group matches on exactly one of name, cidr or attributes. key_groups.[].match.cidr string Matches the devices whose address is in this prefix. Written without host bits, for example 10.0.0.0/8. key_groups.[].match.attributes map of string Matches devices whose inventory attributes equal all of these pairs. key_groups.[].key_ref string The key (a name under keys:) that devices in the group are admitted under. Required. It names the key and never holds it.

docs.title: keys
docs.text: Key Type Description keys.<name>.current.version integer Version number, 1 or greater and unique within the key. The key name is lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. keys.<name>.current.secret_ref secret reference Where the shared secret is read from: env:NAME or file:/absolute/path. Required. The secret itself never appears in this file. port49d reads each version's secret once, when the version comes into force (at start, or in a policy reload that adds it); later reads, at SIGHUP and every 30s, only report a file that has changed or can no longer be read, and port49d keeps the secret it read. A changed secret goes in a new file under a new version. keys.<name>.current.retire_after string Not allowed on the current version or a retired one. On an accept version, the last day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) it still admits; it is refused from midnight after that day. keys.<name>.accept.[].version integer Version number, 1 or greater and unique within the key. The key name is lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. keys.<name>.accept.[].secret_ref secret reference Where the shared secret is read from: env:NAME or file:/absolute/path. Required. The secret itself never appears in this file. port49d reads each version's secret once, when the version comes into force (at start, or in a policy reload that adds it); later reads, at SIGHUP and every 30s, only report a file that has changed or can no longer be read, and port49d keeps the secret it read. A changed secret goes in a new file under a new version. keys.<name>.accept.[].retire_after string Not allowed on the current version or a retired one. On an accept version, the last day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) it still admits; it is refused from midnight after that day. keys.<name>.retired.[].version integer Version number, 1 or greater and unique within the key. The key name is lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. keys.<name>.retired.[].secret_ref secret reference Where the shared secret is read from: env:NAME or file:/absolute/path. Required. The secret itself never appears in this file. port49d reads each version's secret once, when the version comes into force (at start, or in a policy reload that adds it); later reads, at SIGHUP and every 30s, only report a file that has changed or can no longer be read, and port49d keeps the secret it read. A changed secret goes in a new file under a new version. keys.<name>.retired.[].retire_after string Not allowed on the current version or a retired one. On an accept version, the last day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) it still admits; it is refused from midnight after that day.

docs.title: port49-inventory configuration
docs.text:
port49-inventory.yaml configures the inventory service. It is read once at start and strict-decoded; an unknown key, a removed key or a second document is refused, and an error names the line and the kind of fault but never a value. Nothing in the file is a secret: secrets are references (env:NAME or file:/path), and the keys are files.

Every path must be absolute. Durations need a unit, for example 10m. Paths below use [] for an item of a list.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Type Description listen string Required. The API address, host:port, such as 127.0.0.1:8443 or :8443. Mutual TLS on every path. metrics_listen string Address of /metrics, /healthz and /readyz, plain HTTP, carrying no fleet data. Default :9050. webhook_listen string Address that takes NetBox and Nautobot deliveries, host:port, TLS and no client certificate. Set it only if a source has webhook_secret_ref, and a source with webhook_secret_ref needs it. Unset means no webhook. webhook_tls_cert_file string Certificate for the webhook listener. Default: the API's. Set with webhook_tls_key_file. webhook_tls_key_file string Private key for the webhook listener. Set with webhook_tls_cert_file. tls_cert_file string Required. The API's server certificate. tls_key_file string Required. The API's private key. It is read through the key-file check: not a symlink, owned by the service user or root, no group or other mode bits, at most 1 MiB. Keep it in a directory only its owner can write. client_ca_file string Required. The CA that issues the certificates of readers and syncers. readers list of string Identities that may read the bundle: user:<email> in lowercase or a certificate's URI SAN such as spiffe://.... readers or syncers must name someone. syncers list of string Identities that may read the bundle and start a sync (POST /v1/sync). Same form as readers. signing_key_file string Required. The private key that signs the bundle. verify_key_files list of string Further public keys the service accepts for its own state directory and mirror: the old signing key's during a rotation, so the sequence and the bound survive it. The service's own public key is always accepted. Read once, at start, so a change needs a restart: SIGHUP starts a sync and does not re-read it. sync_timeout duration How long one sync may run before it is cut off. Default 5m; 10s to 1h. policy_file string Required. The policy file the service validates a bundle against before serving it. state_dir string Required. Where the service keeps its state. Must not contain or be inside mirror_dir. mirror_dir string Optional. A separate copy of the state, read at a cold start when state_dir has none. Must be outside state_dir. interval duration How often each source is synced unless it sets its own. Default 10m; 1m to 24h.

docs.title: safety
docs.text: Key Type Description safety.max_removed_percent integer The largest share of the fleet, 0 to 100, a sync may remove before it is refused. Default 10. A source without its own bound takes this one.

docs.title: sync
docs.text: Key Type Description sync.[].name string Required. The source's name: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, unique. At least one source is required. sync.[].type string Required. file, netbox or nautobot. sync.[].path string file only, required: the absolute path of the inventory file the source reads. sync.[].interval duration How often this source is synced. Default: the top-level interval; 1m to 24h. sync.[].safety.max_removed_percent integer This source's own removal bound, 0 to 100. Default: the top-level bound. sync.[].url string netbox and nautobot only, required: the product's base URL. sync.[].ca_file string netbox and nautobot only, required: an absolute path to the CA bundle that issues the source's certificate (the host's own bundle file for a public one). sync.[].token_secret_ref secret reference netbox and nautobot only, required: where the API token is read from, env:NAME or file:/absolute/path. One to 512 printable characters with no space. sync.[].webhook_secret_ref secret reference netbox and nautobot only: where the secret that signs this source's webhook deliveries is read from. 32 to 255 printable characters with no space. Needs webhook_listen. sync.[].profile string netbox and nautobot only: the product profile to read with. Must be one the build knows for the type; the error lists them. sync.[].api string netbox and nautobot only: auto (default), graphql or rest. rest cannot give interface addresses. sync.[].page_size integer netbox and nautobot only: devices per request, 1 to 1000. Default 500. sync.[].filter.status string or list of string Statuses kept, a name or a list; an empty list is refused. Default [active]. sync.[].filter.tags list of string Only devices with these tags are kept. sync.[].filter.has_primary_ip boolean Set true to keep only devices that have a primary IP. sync.[].map map of string Attribute name to the path in the product's record it is read from, for example site: site.slug. Must include platform. An attribute name is lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, and not name. sync.[].addresses.primary boolean Whether the device's primary IP is an address. Default true. sync.[].addresses.interfaces list of string Interface names whose addresses are also device addresses. Not with all_interfaces. sync.[].addresses.all_interfaces boolean Set true to take the addresses of every interface. Not with interfaces. At least one of primary, interfaces or all_interfaces must give an address. sync.[].platform_aliases map of string Maps the product's platform slug to the platform name the policy uses, slug: platform_name. Slugs are compared in lowercase; two entries alike in lowercase are refused.

docs.title: port49d configuration
docs.text:
port49d reads port49d.yaml once, at start. port49-broker.yaml is the same schema, read by port49-broker.

A change takes effect at the next restart, with these exceptions, which an entry marks:

  • the policy file and the inventory file, re-read every policy_watch_interval and at SIGHUP
  • inventory.max_removed_percent and inventory.service.verify_key_files, at SIGHUP
  • the tls_listener certificate, key and CA files, every reload_interval and at SIGHUP

The file that a key version's secret_ref names is read once, when the version comes into force: at start, or in a policy reload that adds it. Later reads, at SIGHUP and every 30s, only report a file that has changed or can no longer be read. port49d keeps the secret it read, so a changed secret goes in a new file under a new version.

An unknown key, a second YAML document and a key the loader has removed refuse the start. The error names the line, never the value.

Durations are written with a unit (30s, 15m, 12h). A bare number is refused, except where an entry says 0 is allowed.

Paths are read as written: a relative path resolves against port49d's working directory, not the file's directory.

docs.title: Top-level keys
docs.text: Key Type Description listen string Address of the TACACS+ listener (RFC 8907), host:port. Default :49. The value none turns the listener off, which needs tls_listener: a file with neither listener is refused. Needs a restart. metrics_listen string Address of the metrics, /healthz and /readyz listener. Default :9049. Needs a restart. inventory_file string Path of the device inventory. Exactly one of inventory_file and inventory.service is required. Without a policy the file is read once, at start; with a policy it is re-read at every policy watch and at SIGHUP, and a file that does not load leaves the previous inventory serving. A relative path resolves against port49d's working directory. receipt_idle_ttl duration How long a receipt stays good after its last presentation: each presentation it answers slides the window forward. Default 15m; must be greater than zero and not longer than receipt_max_age. A presentation past either bound is a FAIL on the wire and token_spent in the log. Needs a restart. receipt_max_age duration The longest a receipt lives from its first redemption, however often it is presented. Default 2h; must be greater than zero. Needs a restart. context_idle_ttl duration How long a context with no activity is kept. Default 12h; must be greater than zero. Needs a restart.

docs.title: tls_listener
docs.text: Key Type Description tls_listener.listen string Address of the TACACS+ over TLS 1.3 listener (RFC 9887). Default :300. It may not bind the same address as listen. Needs a restart. tls_listener.cert_file string Server certificate chain, PEM, leaf first. Required, and it must be readable. Re-read every reload_interval and at SIGHUP. tls_listener.key_file string Private key of cert_file. Required. Re-read every reload_interval and at SIGHUP; the key must be owned by port49's user or root, with no group or other mode bit. tls_listener.client_ca_file string The device CA certificates, PEM: the anchors a device certificate must chain to. Required. Re-read every reload_interval and at SIGHUP. tls_listener.intermediates_file string Optional PEM file of issuing CAs held here, so a device that sends only its leaf certificate still verifies. Re-read every reload_interval and at SIGHUP. tls_listener.device_identity.match list of string Which certificate names identify a device: dns_name, ip_address, or both, each at most once. Default both. An empty list is refused. Needs a restart. tls_listener.device_identity.dns_suffixes list of string DNS suffixes a dns_name identity may carry, lower-cased with leading and trailing dots trimmed; letters, digits, - and ., no wildcard. Needs dns_name in match. Needs a restart. tls_listener.server_names list of string When set, the SNI names a ClientHello may ask for: DNS names (lower-cased) and IP addresses (canonical form). A name that looks like an address but is not one in canonical form is refused. Needs a restart. tls_listener.handshake_timeout duration How long a TLS handshake may take. Default 10s; 1s to 30s. Needs a restart. tls_listener.session_ticket_lifetime duration Lifetime of the TLS session tickets the listener issues. Default 0s, which issues none; at most 1h. Needs a restart. tls_listener.reload_interval duration How often the certificate, key, CA and intermediates files are re-read. Default 1m; 10s to 1h. SIGHUP re-reads them at once. A change to this key needs a restart. tls_listener.state_dir string Absolute directory where the listener keeps the certificate revocation lists it verified, in its tls_listener subdirectory, so a restart keeps them. Required when certificate_status.crls names any. Needs a restart. tls_listener.certificate_status.disabled boolean Set true to check no revocation status. Then none of crls, ocsp, refresh_interval and on_unavailable may be set. The block is required: leaving it out is refused, so skipping the check is always a written choice. Needs a restart. tls_listener.certificate_status.crls.[].name string Name of this revocation list source: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, at most 64, and unique in the block. It names the kept file crl-<name>.der and the crl_next_update metric label. tls_listener.certificate_status.crls.[].file string Path of a CRL file. Set exactly one of file and url. tls_listener.certificate_status.crls.[].url string An http or https URL to fetch the CRL from. Set exactly one of file and url. tls_listener.certificate_status.crls.[].issuer_file string Required. The CA certificate that signs the list: the trust anchor, or a certificate the anchor signed. tls_listener.certificate_status.ocsp.responder string An http or https URL of a fixed OCSP responder. Set this or use_aia: true. tls_listener.certificate_status.ocsp.use_aia boolean Set true to ask each certificate's own OCSP responder, from its Authority Information Access extension. Set this or responder. tls_listener.certificate_status.ocsp.timeout duration How long one OCSP request may take. Default 2s; 100ms to 10s. tls_listener.certificate_status.ocsp.hash string The hash of the OCSP CertID: sha256 (default) or sha1. tls_listener.certificate_status.refresh_interval duration How often the revocation lists are fetched or re-read. Default 10m; 1m to 24h. tls_listener.certificate_status.on_unavailable string What to do when a certificate's status cannot be established: refuse (default) refuses the connection, allow admits it and says so. tls_listener.expiry_warning_fraction number A device certificate with less than this fraction of its own lifetime left is named once a day. Default 0.33, the last third of its life; 0 turns the warning off; it must be below 1. Needs a restart.

docs.title: keys
docs.text: Key Type Description keys.<name>.current.version integer Version number of this key, 1 or greater and unique within the key. The key name must be lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, at most 64. This keys: block is for a port49d with no policy; with a policy, the policy file's keys: block replaces it and this one is refused. Needs a restart. keys.<name>.current.secret_ref secret reference Where the shared secret is read from: env:NAME or file:/absolute/path. Required. The secret itself never appears in this file. keys.<name>.current.retire_after string Not allowed on the current version: retire it by making another version current. On an accept version, the last day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) it still admits; midnight after that day it is refused. On a retired version it is refused. keys.<name>.accept.[].version integer Version number of this key, 1 or greater and unique within the key. The key name must be lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, at most 64. This keys: block is for a port49d with no policy; with a policy, the policy file's keys: block replaces it and this one is refused. Needs a restart. keys.<name>.accept.[].secret_ref secret reference Where the shared secret is read from: env:NAME or file:/absolute/path. Required. The secret itself never appears in this file. keys.<name>.accept.[].retire_after string Not allowed on the current version: retire it by making another version current. On an accept version, the last day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) it still admits; midnight after that day it is refused. On a retired version it is refused. keys.<name>.retired.[].version integer Version number of this key, 1 or greater and unique within the key. The key name must be lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, at most 64. This keys: block is for a port49d with no policy; with a policy, the policy file's keys: block replaces it and this one is refused. Needs a restart. keys.<name>.retired.[].secret_ref secret reference Where the shared secret is read from: env:NAME or file:/absolute/path. Required. The secret itself never appears in this file. keys.<name>.retired.[].retire_after string Not allowed on the current version: retire it by making another version current. On an accept version, the last day (UTC, YYYY-MM-DD) it still admits; midnight after that day it is refused. On a retired version it is refused.

docs.title: limits
docs.text: Key Type Description limits.per_nas_connections integer Most simultaneous connections from one device address. Default 32; at least 1. Needs a restart. limits.max_connections integer Global cap on simultaneous connections. Leave it out to size it from the open-file limit at start; otherwise 64 to 1048576. Needs a restart. limits.idle_timeout duration How long a connection may wait for the next packet, and how long a write may take. Default 30s; must be greater than zero. Needs a restart. limits.malformed_backoff_base duration A source that sends a malformed packet is held this long before its connection is closed; each further strike doubles the hold, up to malformed_backoff_max. Default 100ms; must be greater than zero. Needs a restart. limits.malformed_backoff_max duration The ceiling of the malformed-packet hold. Default 5s; must be greater than zero. Needs a restart. limits.malformed_window duration A source's strike count resets when no strike has arrived within this window. Default 10m; zero or negative is refused. Needs a restart. limits.auth_failure_delay_base duration The delay before the FAIL reply to a failed authentication for one device and username; each further failure doubles it, up to auth_failure_delay_max. Default 500ms; must be greater than zero. Needs a restart. limits.auth_failure_delay_max duration The ceiling of the failed-authentication delay. Default 2s; must be greater than zero. Keep it below your devices' shortest TACACS+ reply timeout: a FAIL that arrives after the device gave up reads as an unreachable server, and the device falls back to its local password. Needs a restart. limits.auth_failure_window duration A device and username's failure count resets when no failure has arrived within this window. Default 10m; zero or negative is refused. Needs a restart.

docs.title: accounting
docs.text: Key Type Description accounting.spool_capacity integer Reserved: it must be at least 1, and it does not bound the spool today, which is an append-only durable file. Default 10000. Needs a restart. accounting.spool_path string Path of the accounting spool file. Default /var/lib/port49/acct.jsonl. It may not be the same file as broker.revocations_file. Needs a restart.

docs.title: platforms
docs.text: Key Type Description platforms.<name>.session_services list of string Replaces the built-in list of authorization service values a session on this platform may arrive with. <name> must be a platform port49 ships an adapter for, or the start is refused. A fleet part-way through a service rename lists both names. Omit the key to take the default; an empty list, or an empty string in it, is refused because it would deny every session on that platform. Needs a restart. platforms.<name>.enable_username string Moved to the platforms: block of the policy file, where port49 policy test reads it as port49d does. principal, the default, still loads with a notice; any other value is refused. Delete the line.

docs.title: encryption
docs.text: Key Type Description encryption.current.id string Identifier of the key every token, receipt and context is sealed under at rest, 1 to 64 of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -. It is written into every record the key seals. encryption.current is required. Needs a restart. encryption.current.secret_ref secret reference Where the key's 32 bytes are read from: env:NAME or file:/absolute/path. The secret must be exactly 32 bytes (AES-256). Needs a restart. encryption.previous.id string Identifier of the previous key, kept so records sealed under it still open during a rotation. Optional, and it must differ from encryption.current.id: the id labels each record, so a rotation has to change it. Needs a restart. encryption.previous.secret_ref secret reference Where the previous key's 32 bytes are read from, env:NAME or file:/absolute/path. Naming an id without it is refused. Retire the previous key by removing the block. Needs a restart.

docs.title: session
docs.text: Key Type Description session.grace_window duration How long past session_expires a context is kept: the authorizer denies through it and then deletes the context, and the broker's refresh can resume inside it. Default 10m; must be greater than zero. Needs a restart. session.ceiling_warning_platforms list of string Platforms you add to the list that receive the session-ceiling warning. Each is a platform name: lowercase letters, digits and _, starting with a letter. Not checked against the shipped platform set. Needs a restart. session.index_ttl duration How long the context indexes (principal, session id, certificate) outlive a write. They let a revocation reach a live context. Default 12h; must be greater than zero. Needs a restart. session.max_session_age_default duration The max_session_age a mint uses when the policy names none; session_expires is the authentication time plus this. Default 12h; must be greater than zero. Needs a restart. session.ceiling_warning duration How long before session_expires a permitted reply carries the warning in server_msg. Default 30m; 0s turns the warning off; at most 24h. Needs a restart. session.staleness_ceiling duration A context whose last refresh is older than this is denied context_stale. Default 4h. 0s turns the check off, and every start says so; otherwise at least 1m. With a broker in the same process, broker.refresh_interval may not exceed half of it. Needs a restart.

docs.title: token
docs.text: Key Type Description token.candidate_cap integer How many unspent tokens may stand for one device and username at once. Past it the mint is refused with the count. Default 8; at least 1. Needs a restart.

docs.title: broker
docs.text: Key Type Description broker.listen string Address the broker's HTTPS API listens on. Required when broker is present. Needs a restart. broker.tls_cert_file string The broker's server certificate. Required. Read once, at start. broker.tls_ca_bundle_file string Optional. The CAs clients are to trust for the server certificate, sent on GET /v1/config: the CA in use and, through a rotation, the next. A bundle that does not verify tls_cert_file is not sent. Read once, at start. broker.tls_key_file string The server certificate's private key. Required. It must be owned by port49's user or root, with no group or other mode bit, not a symlink, and at most 1 MiB. Read once, at start. broker.client_ca_file string Shorthand for one x509 human verifier: the one trust anchor client certificates are verified against, which must hold exactly one certificate. Use it or broker.identity, not both; with broker.identity, set trust_anchor_file on the x509 verifier instead. Read once, at start. broker.identity.humans.[].type string Which kind of verifier this is. Under humans: x509, oidc or directory_password. Under machines: x509 (a workload certificate), oidc or k8s. Each type accepts only its own keys; another type's key is refused. broker.identity.humans.[].trust_anchor_file string x509 only: the PEM file of the one trust anchor a chain is verified against. At most one x509 verifier per list, and the two lists may not name the same file. Read once, at start. broker.identity.humans.[].issuer string oidc and k8s: the provider's issuer URL, https with no user information, query or fragment, spelled as the provider spells it in its discovery document. Required. broker.identity.humans.[].client_id string oidc under humans, required: the public client's id, which a person's ID token names in aud. broker.identity.humans.[].principal_claim string oidc under humans, required, with no default: preferred_username, email or upn. Choose the claim only your provider's administrators can set. broker.identity.humans.[].principal_domains list of string oidc and directory_password under humans, required: the domains whose people this verifier may name (user:<name>@<domain>), each a name with a dot and no @, lower-cased. Matched exactly; no subdomain is implied. Two verifiers at different issuers may not share a domain, and a directory_password verifier may not share one with an oidc verifier. broker.identity.humans.[].scopes list of string oidc under humans: extra scopes to request beyond openid, each printable ASCII with no space. broker.identity.humans.[].algorithms list of string oidc and k8s: the token signature algorithms accepted, from RS256, PS256, ES256, ES384 and EdDSA. Default RS256. none and the HS algorithms are refused. broker.identity.humans.[].ca_file string oidc and k8s: PEM CA for the provider's TLS certificate. Optional; without it the system roots are used. It must be a readable file. broker.identity.humans.[].second_factor string directory_password only, required: totp, the one second factor a password sign-in takes. broker.identity.humans.[].filter string directory_password only: an LDAP filter, which must compile, that a person's entry must also match to sign in. broker.identity.humans.[].enrollment.open_until string directory_password only: until this RFC 3339 time (for example 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z), a person with no authenticator enrolled may enroll one by signing in with their directory password. Outside every enrollment window the sign-in is refused. broker.identity.humans.[].enrollment.new_entries_for duration directory_password only: a person whose directory entry was created less than this long ago may enroll. Default 336h (14 days); 0s turns it off; at most 2160h (90 days). broker.identity.humans.[].enrollment.reopen_for duration directory_password only: how long a person's enrollment window stays open after an administrator resets their second factor, and how long reset-second-factor --all reopens enrollment. Default 24h; 1h to 168h. broker.identity.humans.[].rate_limits.failures_per_principal integer directory_password only: failed sign-ins allowed per person within window. Default 5; 1 to 100. broker.identity.humans.[].rate_limits.failures_per_source integer directory_password only: failed sign-ins allowed per source address within window. Default 50; 0 to 10000. broker.identity.humans.[].rate_limits.window duration directory_password only: the window the failure limits count over. Default 15m; 1m to 24h. broker.identity.humans.[].totp_label string directory_password only: the issuer name an authenticator app shows. Printable ASCII, no colon, at most 64 bytes. broker.identity.machines.[].type string Which kind of verifier this is. Under humans: x509, oidc or directory_password. Under machines: x509 (a workload certificate), oidc or k8s. Each type accepts only its own keys; another type's key is refused. broker.identity.machines.[].trust_anchor_file string x509 only: the PEM file of the one trust anchor a chain is verified against. At most one x509 verifier per list, and the two lists may not name the same file. Read once, at start. broker.identity.machines.[].spiffe_trust_domains list of string x509 only, and required: the SPIFFE trust domains whose workloads this anchor may name (spiffe://<trust domain>/<path>), each written as the domain is, never folded to lower case. broker.identity.machines.[].issuer string oidc and k8s: the provider's issuer URL, https with no user information, query or fragment, spelled as the provider spells it in its discovery document. Required. broker.identity.machines.[].audience string Required for oidc (the API identifier a client-credentials token names in aud) and for k8s (the audience your pods' projected token volume asks for). broker.identity.machines.[].clients.[].client_id string oidc only: a client id that may be a machine principal (app:<client id>). Required, and not repeated. broker.identity.machines.[].clients.[].sub string oidc only: the client's own identity at the provider, which its client-credentials tokens carry as sub and no person's token does. Required. broker.identity.machines.[].algorithms list of string oidc and k8s: the token signature algorithms accepted, from RS256, PS256, ES256, ES384 and EdDSA. Default RS256. none and the HS algorithms are refused. broker.identity.machines.[].ca_file string oidc and k8s: PEM CA for the provider's TLS certificate. Optional; without it the system roots are used. It must be a readable file. broker.identity.machines.[].cluster string k8s only, required: this cluster's name in port49's records and log lines.
